title: Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(INTERVAL and PHRASEINT) values are set to a maximum of 365
description: The SETROPTS INTERVAL parameter specifies the system default for the maximum number of days that each user's password and password phrase remain valid. The PHRASEINT parameter specifies the system default for the number of days that each user's password phrase remains valid and overrides the INTERVAL setting for password phrases.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1 Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(INTERVAL and PHRASEINT) values are set to a maximum of 365

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the PASSWORD PROCESSING OPTIONS: section. Look for the following message: PASSWORD CHANGE INTERVAL IS <nnn> DAYS. Verify the value is equal to or less than 254 days. Note: 254 is the maximum value allowed for INTERVAL. Look for the following message: PASSWORD PHRASE CHANGE INTERVAL IS <nnn> DAYS. Verify the value is equal to or less than 365 days. Note: The massage PASSWORD CHANGE INTERVAL IS IN EFFECT FOR PASSWORD PHRASES. may appear instead, indicating that the INTERVAL keyword ... (full steps: CIS section 1.1.1)

remediation.command: To modify the INTERVAL and PHRASEINT parameters use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PASSWORD(INTERVAL(254) PHRASEINT(365))

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(HISTORY) value is set to a minimum of 5
description: HISTORY specifies the number of previous passwords that RACF saves for each user ID and compares with an intended new password. If there is a match with one of the previous passwords, or with the current password, RACF rejects the intended new password. A password history policy prevents users from immediately reusing an old password by enforcing a minimum number of new, unique passwords that must be used before a previous one can be reused.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.2 Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(HISTORY) value is set to a minimum of 5

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the PASSWORD PROCESSING OPTIONS: section. Look for the following message: <nn> GENERATIONS OF PREVIOUS PASSWORDS BEING MAINTAINED. Verify the value is equal to or greater than 5 generations.

remediation.command: To modify the HISTORY parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PASSWORD(HISTORY(5))

title: Ensure that at least one SETROPTS PASSWORD(RULE) is defined with (LENGTH(8) MIXEDALL(1:8))
description: SETROPTS PASSWORD(RULE<n>) specifies up to eight password syntax rules to verify that new passwords meet the installation standards. These rules allow you to control: The minimum and maximum length of passwords The character content of installation-selected positions in the passwords Password composition or complexity requirements are used to increase the strength of a user-created password of a given length.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.3 Ensure that at least one SETROPTS PASSWORD(RULE) is defined with (LENGTH(8) MIXEDALL(1:8))

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the PASSWORD PROCESSING OPTIONS: section. Verify that at least 1 rule in the INSTALLATION PASSWORD SYNTAX RULES: section matches the following value: RULE <n> LENGTH(8) xxxxxxxx

remediation.command: To modify or add a password RULE<n> parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PASSWORD(RULE1(LENGTH(8) MIXEDALL(1:8)))

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(MINCHANGE) value is set to a minimum of 1
description: SETROPTS PASSWORD(MINCHANGE(<nnn>) specifies the number of days that must pass between a user's password and password phrase changes. Users can not change their own passwords and password phrases within the minimum change interval. How frequently a password can be changed should be limited to prevent a user from immediately changing the password multiple times to get back to the original one.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.4 Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(MINCHANGE) value is set to a minimum of 1

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the PASSWORD PROCESSING OPTIONS: section. Look for the following message: PASSWORD MINIMUM CHANGE INTERVAL IS <nnn> DAYS. Verify the value is equal to or greater than 1 days.

remediation.command: To modify the MINCHANGE parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PASSWORD(MINCHANGE(1))

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(REVOKE) value is set to a maximum of 6
description: SETROPTS PASSWORD(REVOKE(<nnn>)) enables you to specify how many consecutive incorrect password and password phrase attempts RACF permits before it revokes the user ID on the next attempt. Note: If you specify REVOKE, INITSTATS must be in effect. The overall goal is it to make it difficult for an attacker to guess a password by trying it against an account, while allowing a user the ability to correct a mistakenly entered password in a reasonable way.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.5 Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(REVOKE) value is set to a maximum of 6

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ATTRIBUTES = section. Verify that INITSTATS appears. Review the command output in the PASSWORD PROCESSING OPTIONS: section. Look for the following message: AFTER <nnn> CONSECUTIVE UNSUCCESSFUL PASSWORD ATTEMPTS, A USERID WILL BE REVOKED. Verify the value is equal to or less than 6 attempts.

remediation.command: To modify the REVOKE parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PASSWORD(REVOKE(6)) If you specify REVOKE, INITSTATS must be in effect. To enable INITSTATS use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS INITSTATS

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(ALGORITHM) value is set to KDFAES
description: The SETROPTS PASSWORD(ALGORITHM) algorithm is used to encrypt passwords and password phrases, but not OIDCARD data. The RACF KDFAES algorithm is designed to be resistant to offline attacks by incorporating the following properties: Each instance of a RACF password injects randomly generated text into the encryption process. This prevents the use of pre-computed password hashes.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.6 Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(ALGORITHM) value is set to KDFAES

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the PASSWORD PROCESSING OPTIONS: section. Verify the following message is present: THE ACTIVE PASSWORD ENCRYPTION ALGORITHM IS KDFAES

remediation.command: To modify the ALGORITHM parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PASSWORD(ALGORITHM(KDFAES)) Note: After ALGORITHM(KDFAES) enablement, the existing algorithm continues to be used to evaluate a user's password or password phrase until the user's password or password phrase is changed. The first time a user's password or password phrase is changed, the new algorithm is used from that point forward. After KDFAES is enabled, you might want to strengthen passwords immediately, rather than wait for users to change them on their normal schedule. The PWCONVERT operand of the ALTUSER command can be used. PWCONVERT converts a DES password and DES password history entries to KDFAES format without requiring the password to be changed. ALTUSER <user-id> PWCONVERT Notes: 1. Conversion assumes that the existing password and password history are in DES format. Do not perform the conversion if you have passwords that are masked or installation-encoded. 2. Conversion does not affect password phrases or phrase history. 3. If an older copy of your RACF database containing DES passwords is compromised and an attacker is able to decrypt a password value, a ... (see CIS section 1.1.6)

title: Ensure SETROPTS PASSWORD(MIXEDCASE) is in effect
description: SETROPTS PASSWORD(MIXEDCASE) indicates that all applications on this system and those that share the RACF database support mixed-case and lowercase passwords. Password composition or complexity requirements are used to increase the strength of a user-created password of a given length.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.9 Ensure SETROPTS PASSWORD(MIXEDCASE) is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the PASSWORD PROCESSING OPTIONS: section. Verify the following messages are present: MIXED CASE PASSWORD SUPPORT IS IN EFFECT

remediation.command: To enable mixed-case and lowercase passwords use the MIXEDCASE parameter of the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PASSWORD(MIXEDCASE)

title: Ensure SETROPTS PASSWORD(SPECIALCHARS) is in effect
description: SETROPTS PASSWORD(SPECIALCHARS) indicates that all applications on this system and those that share the RACF database support additional special characters in passwords. Password composition or complexity requirements are used to increase the strength of a user-created password of a given length.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.10 Ensure SETROPTS PASSWORD(SPECIALCHARS) is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the PASSWORD PROCESSING OPTIONS: section. Verify the following messages are present: SPECIAL CHARACTERS ARE ALLOWED.

remediation.command: To enable additional special characters in passwords use the SPECIALCHARS parameter of the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PASSWORD(SPECIALCHARS)

title: Ensure that LNKAUTH=APFTAB is specified in the IEASYSxx members currently active parmlib data sets
description: Specifying LINKAUTH=APFTAB in the IEASYSxx member(s) currently active PARMLIB data set(s) allows libraries other than those designated as APF to contain authorized modules by adding to this list all libraries in the LNKLST concatenation when accessed as part of the linklist concatenation. Failure to specify LINKAUTH=APFTAB allows libraries other than those designated as APF to contain authorized modules which could bypass security and violate the integrity of the operating system environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.9 Ensure that LNKAUTH=APFTAB is specified in the IEASYSxx members currently active parmlib data sets

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: D IPLINFO Use the following message to determine the xx suffix values for active PARMLIB IEASYSxx members: IEASYS LIST=(xx,..) Check the current PARMLIB IEASYSxx parameters and look for the LNKAUTH parameter. Verify that LNKAUTH=APFTAB.

remediation.command: Update non-compliant entries in PARMLIB IEASYSxx members and re-IPL the system.

title: Ensure that access to DASDVOL and STGADMIN resources are controlled
description: Users responsible for direct access storage device (DASD) administration must be given access to perform necessary functions though profiles in the DASDVOL class (for non-SMS volumes) as well as STGADMIN prefixed profiles in the FACILITY and XFACILIT classes for SMS managed volumes. Failure to properly control and log access to DASD administration resources reduces the integrity and availability of the operating system environment, as well as increases the risk for compromise of confidential data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.1 Ensure that access to DASDVOL and STGADMIN resources are controlled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that DASDVOL and FACILITY and XFACILIT appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that DASDVOL and FACILITY and XFACILIT appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that DASDVOL and FACILITY and XFACILIT appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that: The DASDVOL entry has: o -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- The FACILITY entry ... (full steps: CIS section 2.1.1)

remediation.command: To activate RACF classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(DASDVOL) SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) SETROPTS CLASSACT(XFACILIT) To enable generic profile checking for a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(DASDVOL) SETROPTS GENERIC(FACILITY) SETROPTS GENERIC(XFACILIT) To RACLIST a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(DASDVOL) SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY) SETROPTS RACLIST(XFACILIT) To create catch-all profiles use the RACF RDEFINE command: RDEFINE DASDVOL ** + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('CATCH-ALL PROFILE') PERMIT ** CLASS(DASDVOL) + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(STGADMIN) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(DASDVOL) RDEFINE FACILITY IGG.CATLOCK + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('CONTROLS WHO CAN LOCK/UNLOCK CATALOGS AND WHO CAN ACCESS LOCKED CATALOGS') PERMIT IGG.CATLOCK CLASS(FACILITY) + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(STGADMIN SYSPROG) RDEFINE FACILITY STGADMIN.** + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('STORAGE ADMINISTRATION CATCH-ALL PROFILE') PERMIT STGADMIN.** CLASS(FACILITY) + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(STGADMIN) RDEFINE FACILITY STGADMIN.ADR.STGADMIN.** + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('DFSMSDSS ... (see CIS section 2.1.1)

title: Ensure that access to memory and privileged program dumps is controlled
description: Access to memory and privileged program dumps running Trusted Control Block (TCB) key 0-7 may hold passwords, encryption keys, or other sensitive data that must not be made available. Failure to control access to these facilities could result in unauthorized personnel modifying sensitive z/OS lists.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.12 Ensure that access to memory and privileged program dumps is controlled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the FACILITY entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering the following resources o IEAABD.DMPAKEY o IEAABD.DMPAUTH ... (full steps: CIS section 2.1.12)

remediation.command: To activate RACF classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) To enable generic profile checking for a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(FACILITY) To RACLIST a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY) To create a FACILITY profile use the RACF RDEFINE, PERMIT, and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE FACILITY IEAABD.DMPAKEY + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('DUMP PROGRAMS WITH SYSTEM KEY < 8') PERMIT IEAABD.DMPAKEY CLASS(FACILITY) + ACCESS(READ) ID(SYSPROG) RDEFINE FACILITY IEAABD.DMPAUTH + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DTA('GENERATE PROGRAM DUMPS') PERMIT IEAABD.DMPAUTH CLASS(FACILITY) + ACCESS(UPDATE) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a general resource profile use the RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER FACILITY <profile> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To remove a non-compliant access list entry use the RACF PERMIT and SETROPTS commands: PERMIT <profile> CLASS(FACILITY) + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To remove a non-compliant GAC ... (see CIS section 2.1.12)

title: Ensure that PASSWORD protection for data sets is not used
description: All protection of system resources must come from RACF. If multiple protection mechanisms are in place, the accessibility of data, specifically under contingency plan execution, is subject to compromise.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2.3 Ensure that PASSWORD protection for data sets is not used

audit.command: Interview question to check if system PASSWORD data set and OS passwords are being used.

remediation.command: Migrate from PASSWORD protection for data sets to RACF profiles in the DATASET class.

title: Ensure that access to all APF-authorized objects is controlled
description: The Authorized Program List (APF) designates those libraries that can contain program modules which possess a significant level of security bypass capability. The extattr command can grant the same capability in the UNIX file system, and is secured by the BPX.FILEATTR.APF resource in the FACILITY class.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2.7 Ensure that access to all APF-authorized objects is controlled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY and OPERCMDS appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY and OPERCMDS appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY and OPERCMDS appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering APF data sets Verify that ... (full steps: CIS section 2.2.7)

remediation.command: To activate RACF classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) SETROPTS CLASSACT(OPERCMDS) To enable generic profile checking for a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(FACILITY) SETROPTS GENERIC(OPERCMDS) To RACLIST a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY) SETROPTS RACLIST(OPERCMDS) To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('APF LIBRARY') PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(READ) ID(*) PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To create a FACILITY or OPERCMDS profile use the RACF RDEFINE, PERMIT, and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE FACILITY BPX.FILEATTR.APF + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('ACCESS TO SET APF AUTHORIZATION ON UNIX FILE') PERMIT BPX.FILEATTR.APF CLASS(FACILITY) + ACCESS(READ) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) RDEFINE OPERCMDS MVS.SETPROG + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('SETPROG COMMAND') PERMIT MVS.SETPROG CLASS(OPERCMDS) + ACCESS(UPDATE) ID(SYSPROG) RDEFINE OPERCMDS ... (see CIS section 2.2.7)

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS PROTECTALL value is set to FAIL
description: When PROTECTALL processing is active and set to FAIL, the system automatically rejects any request to create or access a data set that is not RACF-protected. This includes DASD data sets, tape data sets, catalogs, and GDG base names. Temporary data sets that comply with standard MVS temporary data set naming conventions are excluded from PROTECTALL processing.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3.3 Ensure that the SETROPTS PROTECTALL value is set to FAIL

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Verify the following messages are present: PROTECT-ALL IS ACTIVE, CURRENT OPTIONS: PROTECT-ALL FAIL OPTION IS IN EFFECT Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_PROTECTALL_FAIL) Verify the following message is present: IRRH332I SETROPTS PROTECTALL(FAIL) is in effect.

remediation.command: To modify the PROTECTALL parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PROTECTALL(FAILURES)

title: Ensure that the assignment of the UNIX uid(0) is justified
description: RACF user IDs, groups, and started tasks that use z/OS UNIX facilities are defined to RACF with attributes including UID and GID. If these attributes are not correctly defined, data access or command privilege controls could be compromised.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.4 Ensure that the assignment of the UNIX uid(0) is justified

audit.command: Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That user IDs assigned UID(0) in their OMVS segment is justified.

remediation.command: To modify the UID vlaue use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <user-id> OMVS(UID(<number>))

title: Ensure that started tasks defined with the PRIVILEGED attribute is justified
description: Some started tasks require access to a broad set of resources, making it impractical to permit the started task to each of these resources individually. In these cases, the security administrator can choose between assigning the TRUSTED attribute and the PRIVILEGED attribute. A lack of logging can result in loss of visibility as to what protected resources a started task is accessing.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.5 Ensure that started tasks defined with the PRIVILEGED attribute is justified

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACSPT Review the report and for any profiles that have YES in the PRIVILEGED column: Verify that the PRIVILEGED attribute assignment is justified. Note: Examples of PRIVILEGED ... (full steps: CIS section 2.4.5)

remediation.command: To activate RACF classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(STARTED) To enable generic profile checking for a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(STARTED) To RACLIST a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(STARTED) To replace PRIVILEGED with TRUSTED on a STARTED profile use the RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER STARTED <profile> + STDATA(TRUSTED) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(STARTED)

title: Ensure regular audits of AC=1 modules in APF authorized libraries are conducted
description: The AC=1 modules that reside in APF authorized libraries should be reviewed annually. It is important maintain documentation identifying the integrity and justification of vendor APF authorized libraries. For non-vendor APF authorized libraries, the source and documentation identifying the integrity and justification that describes the AC=1 module process should be maintained.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.11 Ensure regular audits of AC=1 modules in APF authorized libraries are conducted

audit.command: Verify the AC=1 documentation and compare it to the actual content of the APF authorized libraries.

remediation.command: Any discrepancy must be fixed: documentation updated and/or libraries/modules removed.

title: Ensure sensitive data sets are encrypted with z/OS data set encryption
description: With z/OS data set encryption, you are able to protect data residing on disk from being viewed by unauthorized users in the clear. Authorization is based on access to the key label that is associated with the data set and used by the access methods to encrypt and decrypt the data. Implementing z/OS dataset encryption ensures that even privileged users, like storage administrators, can manage sensitive data sets without being able to view the contents.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3 Ensure sensitive data sets are encrypted with z/OS data set encryption

audit.command: Request a list of data sets containing sensitive data. Issue the following TSO command for each data set: LISTCAT ALL ENTRIES('<dataset-name>') Review the command output in the ENCRYPTIONDATA section. Verify that the following message appears: DATA SET ENCRYPTION-----(YES) Note: Example acceptable exclusions includes, but is not limited to: The data set is not managed by the Storage Management Subsystem (SMS). The data set type is not supported by data set encryption. Vendor documentation states the data set must not be encrypted (i.e. restrictions documented ... (full steps: CIS section 4.3)

remediation.command: Consult the z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets: Data set encryption manual section for guidance on establishing z/OS data set encryption.

title: Ensure AT-TLS protection is enabled for CSSMTP
description: During the TLS handshake process, mutually acceptable suite of cryptographic algorithms is selected by the server and client. The algorithms specified in the selected suite are used to cryptographically protect the data that subsequently flows between the two. Failure to properly enforce adequate encryption strength could result in the loss of data privacy.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1.3 Ensure AT-TLS protection is enabled for CSSMTP

audit.command: Refer to the CSSMTP configuration file specified on the CONFIG DD statement in the CSSMTP started task JCL. Verify that each TargetServer statement specifies the SECURE YES parameter. Note: For any TargetServer that does not specify SECURE YES, then verify that each JES batch job that sends mail through CSSMTP uses the STARTTLS command to specifically request TLS protection of its outbound mail to the target Message Transfer Agent (MTA).

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating CSSMTP configuration file statements with compliant values.

title: Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs with proper parameters to FTP server started tasks
description: The FTP Server daemon requires special privileges and access to sensitive resources to provide its system services. As such, the data sets the FTP Server daemon relies upon for its configuration, runtime environment and operation must be properly protected from unauthorized modifications or retrieval to ensure system integrity and privacy of sensitive data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2.1 Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs with proper parameters to FTP server started tasks

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACSPT Verify that the FTP Server daemon started task(s) appear in the FROM PROFILES IN THE STARTED CLASS: section and not the FROM THE STARTED PROCEDURES TABLE (ICHRIN03): section. Use ... (full steps: CIS section 6.2.1)

remediation.command: To activate the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(STARTED) To enable generic profile checking for the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(STARTED) To RACLIST the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(STARTED) To create a STARTED profile use the RACF RDEFINE and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE STARTED FTPD*.* + UACC(NONE) + DATA('FTP SERVER DAEMON') + STDATA( + USER(<ftpd-user>) + GROUP(<ftpd-group>) + ) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(STARTED) To make a user ID PROTECTED use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <ftpd-id> + NOPASSWORD + NOPHRASE + NOOIDCARD To modify the OMVS segment for a user ID use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <ftpd-id> + OMVS( + UID(0) + HOME('/') + PROGRAM('/bin/sh') + ) Notes: 1. If the security administrator has defined the SHARED.IDS profile in the UNIXPRIV class, the UID value must be unique. Use the SHARED keyword in addition to UID to assign a value that is already in use. 2. OMVS DIRECTORY and PROGRAM values are case sensitive, so be sure they are entered as-is and not translated to upper case.

title: Ensure startup parameters for the FTP daemon do not allow ANONYMOUS or INACTIVE keywords
description: During initialization, the FTP daemon reads JCL keywords and configuration files to determine values for critical operational parameters. Inappropriate values could result in undesirable operations and degraded security. This exposure may result in unauthorized access impacting data integrity or the availability of some system services.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2.2 Ensure startup parameters for the FTP daemon do not allow ANONYMOUS or INACTIVE keywords

audit.command: Request a copy of all JESJCL of all active site FTP server started tasks. Note: If an FTP server is inactive, review the procedure libraries defined to JES2 and locate the FTP JCL member. Verify that: The following DD statements appear: o SYSTCPD o SYSFTPD If a PARM parameter is specified on the EXEC statement, it must not contain: o The ANONYMOUS keyword or any of it's combinations o The INACTIVE keyword The following instructions are only applicable if a site uses AUTOLOG in any PROFILE.TCPIP TCP/IP profiles to start FTP servers. title: Ensure that the BPXROOT user account is configured with compliant values
description: The z/OS UNIX System Services function setuid can be used to change the UID of the process. When the UID requested is UID=0, the user set as SUPERUSER in BPXPRMxx is used. The default user is BPXROOT. The BPXROOT user must be defined with the correct attributes so the setuid function can be securely used. If these attributes are not correctly defined, data access or command privilege controls could be compromised.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.18 Ensure that the BPXROOT user account is configured with compliant values

audit.command: Request a list of BPXROOT user ID values for the SUPERUSER statement in BPXPRMxx members. Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that the RACF user ID defined as BPXROOT in a SUPERUSER statement: Has the PROTECTED attribute Does not appear on any RACF data set or general resource access list Does not have any segments beyond base and OMVS Does not have any extra system or group privileges (ex. ROAUDIT, CLAUTH, group-JOIN, etc.) Has the following OMVS segment values: o UID value of 0 o HOME value of / o PROGRAM value of ... (full steps: CIS section 9.18)

remediation.command: To create a compliant BPXROOT user ID use the RACF ADDGROUP, ADDUSER, and CONNECT commands: ADDUSER BPXROOT + OWNER(OMVSGRP) + DFLTGRP(OMVSGRP) + NOPASSWORD + DATA('USER IS DEFINED AS SUPERUSER IN BPXPRMXX') + OMVS( + UID(0) SHARED + HOME('/') + PROGRAM('/bin/sh') + ) CONNECT OMVSKERN + GROUP(OMVSGRP) + OWNER(OMVSGRP) Note: The HOME and PROGRAM values are case sensitive. To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT BPX.DAEMON CLASS(FACILITY) + DELETE ID(BPXROOT) SETROPTS RACFLIST GENERIC(FACILITY)

title: Ensure that ability to switch into superuser mode is controlled
description: When a user switches into superuser mode (for example, by issuing the su command in the shell) they operate with an effective UID of 0. That is, they are as privileged as if they were assigned UID(0) in their OMVS segment. Granting access to BPX.SUPERUSER should be viewed to be as sensitive as explicitly assigning UID(0). Erroneous access to BPX.SUPERUSER can result in complete compromise of the system.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.21 Ensure that ability to switch into superuser mode is controlled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the FACILITY entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering the BPX.SUPERUSER resource Request reports generated using ... (full steps: CIS section 9.21)

remediation.command: To activate the FACILITY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) To enable generic profile checking for the FACILITY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(FACILITY) To RACLIST the FACILITY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY) To create a fully-qualified profile use the RACF RDEFINE command: RDEFINE FACILITY BPX.SUPERUSER + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('PERMISSION TO USE THE SU COMMAND TO OBTAIN SUPERUSER AUTHORITY') PERMIT BPX.SUPERUSER CLASS(FACILITY) + ACCESS(READ) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER FACILITY BPX.SUPERUSER + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated ... (see CIS section 9.21)

title: Ensure USS Telnet server is not active
description: Running the USS Telnet server is a security concern as telnet data flow is not encrypted. SSH is recommended. Using an unencrypted network protocol results in clear text passwords being sent across the network connection.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.23 Ensure USS Telnet server is not active

audit.command: The otelnetd server should not be activated through the inet deamon (through /etc/inetd.conf) or permitted in the list of TCPIP services (/etc/services or <hlq>.ETC.SERVICES).

remediation.command: The site will have to follow their standard change management procedure for disabling non-compliant z/OS UNIX deamons.

title: Ensure rlogin is not active
description: The rlogin command enables log in to a remote system and navigate through the remote file system and manipulate its contents, copy files, or execute remote commands. rlogin server processing operates in clear text and therefore should be disabled.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.24 Ensure rlogin is not active

audit.command: The rlogind server should not be activated through the inet deamon (through /etc/inetd.conf) or permitted in the list of TCPIP services (/etc/services or <hlq>.ETC.SERVICES).

remediation.command: The site will have to follow their standard change management procedure for disabling non-compliant z/OS UNIX deamons.

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS RVARYPW values are secured with KDFAES
description: RVARY passwords are used to respond to requests to approve RVARY command processing, where SWITCH is the response to a request to switch RACF databases or change the operating mode of RACF, and STATUS is the response to a request to change RACF or database status from ACTIVE to INACTIVE or from INACTIVE to ACTIVE.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.8 Ensure that the SETROPTS RVARYPW values are secured with KDFAES

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Verify the following messages are present: INSTALLATION DEFINED RVARY SWITCH KDFAES PASSWORD IS IN EFFECT. INSTALLATION DEFINED RVARY STATUS KDFAES PASSWORD IS IN EFFECT.

remediation.command: To modify modify the RVARYPW parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RVARYPW(SWITCH(xxxxx) STATUS(yyyyy) KDFAES) Note: You may use your existing passwords. SETROPTS does not keep a history for RVARY passwords.

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS INACTIVE value is set to a maximum of 45
description: PASSWORD(INACTIVE(<nnn>)) command specifies the number of days (1 - 255) that a user ID can remain unused and still be considered valid. RACF user verification checks the number of days since the last successful time the user accessed the system against the INACTIVE value and, if the former is larger, revokes the user's right to use the system.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1 Ensure that the SETROPTS INACTIVE value is set to a maximum of 45

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ATTRIBUTES = section. Verify that INITSTATS appears. Look for the following message: INACTIVE USERIDS ARE BEING AUTOMATICALLY REVOKED AFTER <nnn> DAYS. Verify the value is equal to or less than 45 days.

remediation.command: To modify the INACTIVE parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS INACTIVE(45) Notes: 1. INACTIVE does not apply to Protected user IDs. Protected user IDs are protected from being revoked through inactivity. 2. If the backup database is needed but does not contain current information, some user IDs can be revoked because they appear to have been unused beyond the number of days specified on the INACTIVE operand. For more information, see z/OS Security Server RACF System Programmer's Guide. If you specify INACTIVE, INITSTATS must be in effect. To enable INITSTATS use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS INITSTATS

title: Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs to started tasks
description: Started procedures have system generated job statements that do not contain the user, group, or password statements. To enable the started procedure to access the same protected resources that users and groups access, started procedures must have an associated user ID. If a user ID is not associated with the started procedure, the started procedure will not have access to the resources.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.2 Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs to started tasks

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACSPT Review the FROM PROFILES IN THE STARTED CLASS: section. Verify that no entries contain: -USER NOT SPECIFIED, ICHRIN03 WILL BE USED- Request IRRUT100 cross reference output and ... (full steps: CIS section 1.2.2)

remediation.command: Notes: 1. RACF cannot be initialized if ICHRIN03 is not present so even when a catch-all ** profile in the STARTED class is used to assign user IDs, a dummy ICHRIN03 is shipped with and installed by RACF. 2. For installations that have an existing ICHRIN03 in place and want to migrate to using the STARTED class, a sample REXX exec is provided in member ICHSPTCV in SYS1.SAMPLIB to process the output of the RACF DSMON program and build RACF RDEFINE commands to replicate current ICHRIN03 entries. 3. It is recommended that a minimal set of STC definitions be maintained in the ICHRIN03, such that an IPL can be completed and the system can be brought up in cases of RACF failure. To activate the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(STARTED) To enable generic profile checking for the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(STARTED) To RACLIST the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(STARTED) To create dedicated IDs for the STDATA segment use the RACF ADDGROUP, ADDUSER, and CONNECT commands: ADDGROUP STCGRP + OWNER(<group>) + SUPGROUP(<group>) + DATA('CATCH-ALL STC PROFILE GROUP') ADDUSER ... (see CIS section 1.2.2)

title: Ensure user propagation is controlled
description: Batch jobs that are user-submitted to the operating system should inherit the user ID of the submitter. This will identify the batch job with the user for the purpose of accessing resources. Jobs submitted without the USER operand specified on the JOB statement which run under a user ID other than the user submitting the job present a security violation in that the issuer of the job will inherit the authority of the user ID and may allow ...
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.3 Ensure user propagation is controlled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that PROPCNTL appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that PROPCNTL appears. Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that all user IDs that require propagation control have a dedicated profile in the PROPCNTL class.

remediation.command: To activate the PROPCNTL class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(PROPCNTL) To RACLIST the PROPCNTL class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(PROPCNTL) To create a PROPCNTL profile use the RACF RDEFINE and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE PROPCNTL <user-id> SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(PROPCNTL) Note: 1. For a profile in the PROPCNTL class, RACF checks only for the presence or absence of a profile in this class. If a profile exists for a particular user ID, user ID propagation does not occur for that user ID. 2. RACF performs no logging and issues no messages for profiles in the PROPCNTL class. 3. PROPCNTL profiles only control propagation for local jobs. If the installation uses &RACLNDE for its remote nodes, only the PROPCNTL profiles are necessary. For more information on the use of &RACLNDE, see Defining nodes as local input sources. If the installation uses NODES profiles, it must also use them to control propagation (see Controlling user ID propagation in an NJE environment). 4. If you have controlled a user ID using the PROPCNTL class, and that user wants to submit a batch job to run from that user ID, the JOB statement must ... (see CIS section 1.2.3)

title: Ensure that started tasks defined with the TRUSTED attribute are justified
description: The TRUSTED attribute allows a started task to bypass RACF checking. It is vital that this attribute is not granted to unauthorized started tasks which could then obtain unauthorized access to the system. Unauthorized started tasks obtaining unauthorized access to the system could result in the compromise of the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the operating system, RACF, or customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.4 Ensure that started tasks defined with the TRUSTED attribute are justified

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACSPT Review the report and for any profiles that have YES in the TRUSTED column: Verify that the TRUSTED attribute assignment is justified. Note: Examples of TRUSTED assignment justification includes, but is not limited to: The started task or address space creates or accesses a wide variety of unpredictably named data sets. Insufficient authority to an accessed resource might risk an unsuccessful IPL or other critical system functionality error. It is listed as a requirement by the product documentation or vendor.

remediation.command: To remove the TRUSTED from a STARTED profile use the RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER STARTED <profile> + STDATA(NOTRUSTED) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(STARTED) IBM provides guidance on z/OS started tasks and address spaces that require TRUSTED in the MVS Initialization and Tuning Reference, linked in the additional information section.

title: Ensure that the OPERCMDS resource class is enabled
description: SETROPTS CLASSACT(OPERCMDS) specifies that the class OPERCMDS will have RACF protection is to be in effect for it. These values become effective immediately after the command SETROPTS CLASSACT(OPERCMDS) is issued. If no setting is found, the system-wide defaults will be used. The improper setting of any subsystem fields, individually or in combination with another, can compromise the security of the processing environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.5 Ensure that the OPERCMDS resource class is enabled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that OPERCMDS appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that OPERCMDS appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that OPERCMDS appears.

remediation.command: To activate the OPERCMDS class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(OPERCMDS) To enable generic profile checking for the OPERCMDS class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(OPERCMDS) To RACLIST the OPERCMDS class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(OPERCMDS)

title: Ensure that the CONSOLE resource class is enabled
description: MCS consoles can be used to issue operator commands. Failure to control access to MCS consoles could result in unauthorized personnel issuing sensitive operator commands. Failure to control access to MCS consoles could result in unauthorized personnel issuing sensitive operator commands. This may threaten the integrity and availability of the operating system environment and compromise the confidentiality of customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.6 Ensure that the CONSOLE resource class is enabled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that CONSOLE appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that CONSOLE appears.

remediation.command: To activate the CONSOLE class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(CONSOLE) To RACLIST the CONSOLE class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(CONSOLE)

title: Ensure that the FACILITY resource class is enabled
description: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) specifies that the class FACILITY class is active and that RACF protection is to be in effect for it. These values become effective immediately after the command SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) and SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY) are issued. If no setting is found, the system-wide defaults will be used. The improper setting of any subsystem fields, individually or in combination with another, can compromise the security of the processing environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.7 Ensure that the FACILITY resource class is enabled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears.

remediation.command: Note: The FACILITY class can be used for a wide variety of purposes depending on the products installed on your system. Care must be taken when enabling the class for the first time. To activate the FACILITY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) To enable generic profile checking for the FACILITY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(FACILITY) To RACLIST the FACILITY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY)

title: Ensure that inapplicable PPT entries have been invalidated
description: The program properties table (PPT) contains entries for special attributes of programs. One of these entries indicates whether or not the program is allowed to bypass datasets password protection (PPTNOPAS), or access key protected storage. If invalid or inapplicable PPT entries exist, a venue is provided for the introduction of Trojan Horse modules with security bypass capabilities.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.8 Ensure that inapplicable PPT entries have been invalidated

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM SYSPPT Verify that each privileged PROGRAM NAME entry is valid. Note: To determine if a program entry is valid issue the following TSO command: ISRDDN LOAD <privileged-module> If the return message is Load Failed the entry can be considered invalid.

remediation.command: Although you cannot remove entries from the PPT, you can create the effect of removing an entry from the PPT by defining the program name in the PARMLIB member SCHEDxx without special attributes. This statement overrides the existing entry in the PPT, and causes any APF-authorized program with a matching name to run with the same attributes as a problem program. Update the SCHEDxx member: PPT PGMNAME(<privileged-module>) Notes: If you specify more than one PPT statement with the same program name, the systems accept only the first occurrence of the name and issues error message IEF732I for all subsequent occurrences of that name. When referring to a DD statement, the system does not honor requests for special properties as defined in the PPT.

title: Ensure that the CONSOLxx members are configured
description: MCS consoles can be used to issue operator commands. This exposure may threaten the integrity and availability of the operating system environment and compromise the confidentiality of customer data. Failure to control access to MCS consoles could result in unauthorized personnel issuing sensitive operator commands.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.10 Ensure that the CONSOLxx members are configured

audit.command: Review the current PARMLIB CONSOLxx members. Verify that the DEFAULT statement for each CONSOLxx member specifies LOGON(REQUIRED). Note: At the discretion of the site ISSO LOGON(AUTO) may be used. If LOGON(AUTO) is used verify that the console user IDs are defined with minimal access. Verify that the CONSOLE statement for each console: Assigns a unique name using the NAME parameter. Specifies a default authority of INFO using the AUTH parameter. Exceptions: o The AUTH parameter is not valid for consoles defined with UNIT(PRT). o The system console is ... (full steps: CIS section 1.2.10)

remediation.command: Update non-compliant entries in PARMLIB CONSOLxx members and re-IPL the system.

title: Ensure that no expired digital certificates are used
description: When an X.509 certificate stored in RACF has the TRUST or HIGHTRUST status, it can be used by RACF for its intended purpose (map to a user ID, or treat as a trusted certificate authority or trusted site). X.509 certificates expire to prevent prolonged use of potentially compromised private keys and outdated cryptographic algorithms, ensuring that security infrastructure remains up-to-date against evolving threats and that the information within the ...
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.11 Ensure that no expired digital certificates are used

audit.command: Note: Certificates used for password enveloping can continue to be used after expiring and should not be removed if password enveloping is still active. Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that each certificate with a TRUST or HIGHTRUST status is not expired. Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRATION) Verify that the health check returns this message: IRRH277I No exceptions are detected. Expired ... (full steps: CIS section 1.2.11)

remediation.command: Note: Certificates used for password enveloping can continue to be used after expiring and should not be removed if password enveloping is still active. Follow site procedures for certificate life cycle management.

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS RVARYPW are set to non- default values
description: The SETROPTS RVARYPW([SWITCH(switch-pw)][STATUS(status-pw)]) command specifies the passwords that the operator is to use to respond to requests to approve RVARY command processing, where switch-pw is the response to a request to switch RACF databases or change the operating mode of RACF, and status-pw is the response to a request to change RACF or database status from ...
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.12 Ensure that the SETROPTS RVARYPW are set to non- default values

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Verify the following messages are present: INSTALLATION DEFINED RVARY PASSWORD IS IN EFFECT FOR THE SWITCH FUNCTION. INSTALLATION DEFINED RVARY PASSWORD IS IN EFFECT FOR THE STATUS FUNCTION.

remediation.command: To modify the RVARYPW values use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RVARYPW(SWITCH(<password>)) SETROPTS RVARYPW(STATUS(<password>))

title: Ensure that RACF default user ID IBMUSER is disabled
description: The default IBMUSER user ID is intended for use only during the initial RACF installation process. After installation, the IBMUSER user ID should be revoked so that it cannot be used by unauthorized users.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.13 Ensure that RACF default user ID IBMUSER is disabled

audit.command: Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That the IBMUSER user ID: Has the REVOKE status Has the PROTECTED attribute Has the RESTRICTED attribute Has the UAUDIT attribute Does not appear on any RACF data set or general resource access list Does not have any segments beyond base (ex. no OMVS segment) Does not have any extra system or group privileges (ex. SPECIAL, OPERATIONS, group-JOIN, etc.)

remediation.command: To adjust IBMUSER properties use the ALTUSER and CONNECT commands: ALTUSER IBMUSER + NOPASSWORD + RESTRICTED + UAUDIT + REVOKE + NOSPECIAL + NOAUDIT + NOPERATIONS + NOROAUDIT + NOTSO + NOOMVS + NOCICS CONNECT IBMUSER + GROUP(group) + AUTHORITY(USE) + NOAUDITOR + NOOPERATIONS + NOSPECIAL To remove IBMUSER from an access list entry use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT <profile> CLASS(<class>) + DELETE ID(IBMUSER)

title: Ensure that the use of RACF SPECIAL attribute is justified
description: The SPECIAL user attribute allows full authorization to modify all profiles in RACF database and allows the user to perform all RACF functions, except those requiring AUDITOR or ROAUDIT attributes. The group-SPECIAL attribute allows decentralized RACF control of datasets and resources. Users with SPECIAL privilege can alter any profile and give themselves permissions to alter data, including logging and audit data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.1 Ensure that the use of RACF SPECIAL attribute is justified

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACUSR Review the SPECIAL column under the ATTRIBUTE TYPE grouping. Verify when SYSTEM or GROUP appears if the assignment is justified for the user.

remediation.command: To remove the SPECIAL attribute use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <user-id> NOSPECIAL To remove group-SPECIAL authority use the RACF CONNECT command: CONNECT <user-id> + GROUP(<group>) + NOSPECIAL

title: Ensure that SYS1.UADS contains only recovery user IDs
description: SYS1.UADS is a dataset where user IDs are be maintained with applicable password information for whenever RACF is not functional. If an unauthorized user has access to SYS1.UADS they could enter their user ID and password into the SYS1.UADS dataset and could give themselves access to the system.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.2 Ensure that SYS1.UADS contains only recovery user IDs

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: ACCOUNT Issue the following ACCOUNT sub-command to list all entries in SYS1.UADS: LIST (*) Verify that only recovery IDs are defined in SYS1.UADS. If there are recovery IDs defined in SYS1.UADS, request IRRUT100 cross reference output and reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that the recovery user IDs defined in SYS1.UADS have a paired RACF user ID with limited privileges: User ID has the PROTECTED attribute User ID has the RESTRICTED attribute User ID has the UAUDIT attribute User ID has ... (full steps: CIS section 1.3.2)

remediation.command: To remove a user ID from SYS1.UADS use the TSO ACCOUNT-DELETE subcommand: ACCOUNT DELETE (<user-id>) END Use the RACONVRT command if needed as an aid in converting users from SYS1.UADS to the RACF database: RACONVRT INCLUDE USERID(userid) Notes: If RACF is installed and active, you require RACF SPECIAL authority to issue the command. RACONVRT generates the RACF commands needed to update or create RACF user profiles, and places these commands into members of a partitioned data set. This data set, <prefix>.IKJ.RACONVRT.CLIST, contains the commands necessary to convert to the RACF data base. RACONVRT creates, but does not execute the RACF commands; therefore, you can edit and change the data set's members to customize the conversion process before issuing the RACF commands. To modify RACF entries for recovery user IDs use the RACF ALTUSER or CONNECT commands: ALTUSER <user-id> + NOPASSWORD + RESTRICTED + UAUDIT + REVOKE + NOSPECIAL + NOAUDIT + NOPERATIONS + NOROAUDIT + NOTSO + NOOMVS + NOCICS CONNECT <user-id> + GROUP(<group>) + AUTHORITY(USE) + NOAUDITOR + NOOPERATIONS + NOSPECIAL To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command ... (see CIS section 1.3.2)

title: Ensure that MCS console user IDs are protected
description: MCS consoles can be used to issue operator commands. When using the LOGON(AUTO) control, a user with the name of the MCS console will be used for access checking. Failure to control access to MCS consoles could result in unauthorized personnel issuing sensitive operator commands.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.3 Ensure that MCS console user IDs are protected

audit.command: Review the current PARMLIB CONSOLxx members. For each console name found request IRRUT100 cross reference output and reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that the <console-name> has been defined in RACF as a user ID with limited privileges: Have the PROTECTED attribute Have the RESTRICTED attribute Does not have any segments beyond base (ex. no OMVS segment) Does not have any extra system or group privileges (ex. ROAUDIT, CLAUTH, group-JOIN, etc.) Does not appear on any RACF data set or general resource access lists. ... (full steps: CIS section 1.3.3)

remediation.command: To create dedicated IDs for consoles named in CONSOLxx use the RACF ADDGROUP, ADDUSER, and CONNECT commands: ADDGROUP CONGRP + OWNER(<group>) + SUPGROUP(<group>) + DATA('DEFAULT CONSOLE OWNING GROUP') ADDUSER <console-name> + OWNER(CONGRP) + DFLTGRP(CONGRP) + NOPASSWORD + RESTRICTED + DATA('MCS CONSOLE ID') CONNECT <console-name> + GROUP(CONGRP) + OWNER(CONGRP) To create a paired profiles in the OPERCMDS and CONSOLE classes use the RACF RDEFINE and PERMIT commands: RDEFINE OPERCMDS MVS.MCSOPER.<console-name> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('EXTENDED MCS CONSOLE ACCESS') + NOWARNING PERMIT OPERCMDS MVS.MCSOPER.<console-name> + ACCESS(READ) ID(<console-name>) RDEFINE CONSOLE <console-name> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING PERMIT CONSOLE <console-name> + ACCESS(READ) ID(<console-name>) Notes: 1. Depending on the RACF class settings you may be required to issue a RACF SETROPTS REFRESH command for updates to be effective. 2. You cannot specify the WHEN operand on the RDEFINE and RALTER commands for profiles in the CONSOLE class. 3. After you define a console in the CONSOLE class and protect it with a UACC of NONE, no one can log ... (see CIS section 1.3.3)

title: Ensure that STARTED resource class profiles assign PROTECTED user IDs
description: PROTECTED user IDs are protected from being used to logon to the system and from being revoked through inactivity or unsuccessful attempts to access the system using incorrect passwords and password phrases. However, they can be revoked using the ALTUSER REVOKE command. We recommend assigning PROTECTED user IDs to z/OS UNIX, and to the UNIX daemons, started procedures, applications, servers or subsystems associated with z/OS UNIX, to minimize their exposure to inadvertent or malicious misuse or revocation.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.4 Ensure that STARTED resource class profiles assign PROTECTED user IDs

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACSPT Use the ASSOCIATED USER column to generate the list of user IDs to review. Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that the started task RACF user ID: Has the PROTECTED attribute

remediation.command: To make a user ID PROTECTED use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <user-id> + NOPASSWORD + NOPHRASE + NOOIDCARD

title: Ensure that the assignment of RACF CLAUTH authority is justified
description: Users receive the CLAUTH attribute on a class-by-class basis. If a user has the CLAUTH attribute in a class, or in a class that shares the same POSIT value in the class descriptor table (CDT), RACF allows the user to utilize a subset of commands for delegated administration of profiles in that class.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.5 Ensure that the assignment of RACF CLAUTH authority is justified

audit.command: Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to identify user IDs with CLAUTH authority. Verify if the assignment is justified for the user.

remediation.command: To remove CLAUTH authority the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <user-id> NOCLAUTH(<class-name>)

title: Ensure that access to active SMF collection files is controlled
description: SMF data collection is the system activity journaling facility of the z/OS system. With the proper parameter designations, it serves as the basis to ensure individual user accountability. SYS1.MANxx datasets should be created once and reused when cleared. Users may have UPDATE access to the datasets, but ALTER allows for dataset deletion and should be avoided. ALTER access reduces the integrity and availability of the operating system environment and reduces compromises of confidential customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.2 Ensure that access to active SMF collection files is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entry covering SYS1.MANxx datasets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that SYS1.MANxx data sets are secured by RACF profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(UPDATE) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access READ and higher permits are restricted to: o Systems Programmers o IDs authorized to access these resources at this level

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD 'SYS1.MAN*' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('SMF COLLECTION FILES') PERMIT 'SYS1.MAN*' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD 'SYS1.MAN*' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT 'SYS1.MAN*' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS WHEN(PROGRAM) value is active
description: SETROPTS WHEN(PROGRAM) activates RACF program control, which includes both access control to load modules and program access to data sets. To set up access control to load modules, you must identify your controlled programs by creating a profile for each in the PROGRAM class. Not protecting critical programs and not ensuring a clean address space can compromise the security of the processing environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.3 Ensure that the SETROPTS WHEN(PROGRAM) value is active

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ATTRIBUTES = section. Look for the following message: WHEN(PROGRAM -- BASIC) Verify that the message appears. Note: The message may specify BASIC, ENHANCED-WARNING, or ENHANCED. This is determined by the IRR.PGMSECURITY profile in the FACILITY resource class, and the specific value in the message is not relevant for this control.

remediation.command: To modify the WHEN(PROGRAM) parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS WHEN(PROGRAM)

title: Ensure that access to the ICHDSM00 (DSMON) program is controlled
description: ICHDSM00 is the data security monitor utility (DSMON). READ authority to this program in the PROGRAM class is one way a user can have authority to run the utility. RACF ships the utility in SYS1.LINKLIB. ICHDSM00 provides information on the security posture of the system. Such information should not be available to general users.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.4 Ensure that access to the ICHDSM00 (DSMON) program is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the PROGRAM entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entry covering the ICHDSM00 resource Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that a ICHDSM00 profile in the PROGRAM class is defined and: Has a UACC of NONE Is not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(READ) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access READ and higher permits are restricted to: o Auditors o Security Administrators o Systems Programmers o IDs ... (full steps: CIS section 2.1.4)

remediation.command: To create a PROGRAM profile use the RACF RDEFINE and PERMIT commands: RDEFINE PROGRAM ICHDSM00 + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + ADDMEM('SYS1.LINKLIB'//NOPADCHK) + DATA('DATA SECURITY MONITOR UTILITY (DSMON)') PERMIT ICHDSM00 CLASS(PROGRAM) + ACCESS(READ) ID(AUDITOR SECADMIN SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH WHEN(PROGRAM) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a general resource profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER PROGRAM ICHDSM00 + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH WHEN(PROGRAM) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT ICHDSM00 CLASS(PROGRAM) + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH WHEN(PROGRAM) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH ... (see CIS section 2.1.4)

title: Ensure that access to the IRRDPI00 program is controlled
description: ICHDPI00 is the program that is used to update the dynamic parse function in RACF, and to refresh in-storage custom field data after making updates in the CFIELD class. READ authority to this program in the PROGRAM class is one way a user can have authority to run the program. RACF ships the program in SYS1.LINKLIB.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.5 Ensure that access to the IRRDPI00 program is controlled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify FACILITY appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that: The FACILITY entry has: o -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entry covering the IRRDPI00 resource The PROGRAM entry has: o -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ... (full steps: CIS section 2.1.5)

remediation.command: To activate RACF classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) To enable generic profile checking for a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(FACILITY) To RACLIST a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY) To create a PROGRAM profile use the RACF RDEFINE, PERMIT, and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE PROGRAM IRRDPI00 + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + ADDMEM('SYS1.LINKLIB'//NOPADCHK) + DATA('UPDATE RACF DYNAMIC PARSE FUNCTION') PERMIT IRRDPI00 CLASS(PROGRAM) + ACCESS(READ) ID(SECADMIN SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH WHEN(PROGRAM) To create a FACILITY profile use the RACF RDEFINE, PERMIT, and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE FACILITY IRRDPI00 + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('UPDATE RACF DYNAMIC PARSE FUNCTION') PERMIT IRRDPI00 CLASS(FACILITY) + ACCESS(READ) ID(SECADMIN SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a general resource profile use the RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER PROGRAM IRRDPI00 + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH WHEN(PROGRAM) RALTER FACILITY IRRDPI00 + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + NOWARNING ... (see CIS section 2.1.5)

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS ERASE value is set to ALL
description: SETROPTS ERASE(ALL) specifies that data management is to erase all scratched data sets including temporary data sets. NOERASE specifies that no DASD data sets are erased when deleted. The system-wide options control the default settings for determining how RACF will function when handling requests for access to the operating system environment, RACF, and customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.6 Ensure that the SETROPTS ERASE value is set to ALL

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output and look for the following message: ERASE-ON-SCRATCH IS ACTIVE, CURRENT OPTIONS: ERASE-ON-SCRATCH FOR ALL DATA SETS IS IN EFFECT Verify that the message appears. Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_ERASE_ON_SCRATCH) Verify that the health check returns this message for each system: IRRH338I SETROPTS ERASE(ALL) is in effect.

remediation.command: To modify the ERASE parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS ERASE(ALL)

title: Ensure that the TEMPDSN class is active
description: The TEMPDSN class provides protection for temporary data sets if these data sets are not deleted by the job or session which created them. These values become effective immediately after the command SETROPTS CLASSACT(TEMPDSN) is issued. You can protect temporary data sets. Normally, these data sets are considered protected from any accesses except by the job or session that created them, and therefore do not need to be protected by RACF.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.7 Ensure that the TEMPDSN class is active

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that TEMPDSN appears. Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_TEMPDSN_ACTIVE) Verify that the health check returns this message: IRRH228I The class TEMPDSN is active.

remediation.command: To activate the TEMPDSN class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(TEMPDSN)

title: Ensure that access to RACF database data sets is controlled
description: RACF database files contain all access control information for the operating system environment and system resources as well as user registry, user permissions and user authentication data (including encrypted passwords and passphrases), private X.509 certificate keys, and more. An unsecured RACF database poses significant risks, including unauthorized access to sensitive data, system compromise, and potential operational disruption, due to the comprehensive access control information it stores.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.8 Ensure that access to RACF database data sets is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering RACF primary and backup databases as well as any copies Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that the RACF primary and backup databases as well as any copies are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(READ) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access READ permits are ... (full steps: CIS section 2.1.8)

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD 'SYS1.RACF.*' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('RACF DTABASE') PERMIT 'SYS1.RACF.*' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD 'SYS1.RACF.*' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT 'SYS1.RACF.*' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure that access to the RACF remote sharing facility data sets is controlled
description: When using the RACF remote sharing facility (RRSF) to propagate RACF requests across the network, each node in the configured network has a pair of VSAM files (INMSG and OUTMSG) to save queued work until it is sent, and its receipt is confirmed by the remote node. These files must be protected. Disclosure of this information can compromise user credentials and give clues to the protection mechanisms in effect.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.9 Ensure that access to the RACF remote sharing facility data sets is controlled

audit.command: Note: The subsystem-prefix must be supplied by the site. For example if a site has chosen "@" then the command would be @TARGET. Issue the following TSO command: <subsystem-prefix>TARGET LIST NODE(*) Review the command output in the FILE USAGE section to determine the RRSF workspace data sets to be evaluated. Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_RRSF_RESOURCES) To obtain a list of RRSF workspace data sets. Issue the following TSO command for each RRSF workspace ... (full steps: CIS section 2.1.9)
