To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH ... (see CIS section 2.1.9)

title: Ensure that access to the RACF parameter library is controlled
description: The started procedure in SYS1.PROCLIB that starts the RACF subsystem address space contains an optional RACFPARM DD statement that identifies a file containing commands to run during subsystem initialization. This file must be protected with a DATASET profile. When these commands execute, they do so under the identity associated with the RACF subsystem, and OPERCMDS checking is not performed. Anyone with UPDATE access can insert commands.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.10 Ensure that access to the RACF parameter library is controlled

audit.command: Request a list of any and all RACF parameter library data sets referenced by the RACFPARM DD. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering the RACF parameter library data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That the RACF parameter library data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(UPDATE) and ... (full steps: CIS section 2.1.10)

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD 'SYS1.RACF.PARM' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('RACF PARAMETER LIBRARY') PERMIT 'SYS1.RACF.PARM' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD 'SYS1.RACF.PARM' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT 'SYS1.RACF.PARM' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH ... (see CIS section 2.1.10)

title: Ensure that RACF remote sharing connections use the TCP/IP protocol
description: Each individual RACF remote sharing (RRSF) connection to a remote node can use either the original APPC protocol or the newer TCP/IP protocol. APPC can only use DES-based encryption, which is far weaker than the encryption offered by TCP/IP.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.11 Ensure that RACF remote sharing connections use the TCP/IP protocol

audit.command: Note: The subsystem-prefix must be supplied by the site. For example if a site has chosen "@" then the command would be @TARGET. Issue the following TSO command: <subsystem-prefix>TARGET LISTPROTCOL Verify that the string APPC does not appear in the resulting IRRM009I messages.

remediation.command: Consult the z/OS Security Server RACF System Programmer's Guide for guidance on modifying and securing RRSF connections.

title: Ensure that access to system TRACE data sets is controlled
description: SYS1.TRACE is used to trace and debug system problems. It can contain sensitive information. In fact, this same consideration applies to any sort of trace log, many of which are application specific. Unauthorized access to TRACE data sets can divulge sensitive system information.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.13 Ensure that access to system TRACE data sets is controlled

title: Ensure that access to system backup data sets is controlled
description: System backup data sets are necessary for recovery of DASD resident data sets. Update access to System backup files is limited to system programmers and/or batch jobs that perform DASD backups. Unauthorized access could result in the compromise of the operating system environment, RACF, and customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.14 Ensure that access to system backup data sets is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering system backup data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That the system backup data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(READ) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access READ and higher permits are restricted to: o Systems Programmers o IDs ... (full steps: CIS section 2.1.14)

To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure that access to system DUMP data sets is controlled
description: System DUMP data sets are used to record system data areas and virtual storage associated with system task failures. Unauthorized access could result in the compromise of the operating system environment, RACF, and customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1.15 Ensure that access to system DUMP data sets is controlled

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS TERMINAL value is set to NONE
description: SETROPTS TERMINAL is used to set the universal access authority (UACC) associated with undefined terminals. The improper setting of this field can compromise the security of the z/OS environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3.1 Ensure that the SETROPTS TERMINAL value is set to NONE

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS GENERIC is enabled for ACTIVE classes
description: SETROPTS GENERIC controls what classes may have generic profiles. Generic profiles are profiles which cover zero or more resources. They substantially simplify security administration. Note: It is possible to have characters that would be considered "wildcards" such as *, %, $, and & in non-generic profiles.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3.2 Ensure that the SETROPTS GENERIC is enabled for ACTIVE classes

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that active classes appear, with the following exceptions: Any class which is defined with any of the following attributes as documented in the Security Server RACF Macros and Interfaces reference: o GENERIC=DISALLOWED o GROUP o PROFDEF=NO Any class defined as "generics not recommended" in the Security Server RACF Command Language Reference, including but not limited to: o CDT o CFIELD o DIGTCERT o DIGTRING o IDIDMAP o KERBLINK o REALM o ... (full steps: CIS section 2.3.2)

remediation.command: To enable GENERIC for a class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(<class>) Guidelines: If you have GENERIC turned on for the DIGTCERT class when the certificate is created or added and its Issuer's Distinguished Name contains any generic characters (*, & and %), a generic certificate profile will be created. This generic feature will cause unexpected behavior when the certificate is being used by other programs. You need to remove it add it back after turning off GENERIC in the DIGTCERT class. If a general resource class already has discrete profiles with names that contain generic characters (*, &, and %), enabling generic profile checking for the class prevents RACF from using those discrete profiles for authorization checking. In general, once you activate generic profile checking for a class and define generic profiles, avoid deactivating it with the NOGENERIC operand. RACF will not use your previously defined generic profiles for authorization checking while NOGENERIC is in effect.

title: Ensure that ALTER access authority in DISCRETE profiles is limited
description: When a RACF profile is a DISCRETE profile the ALTER level of access not only grants access to the resources protected by the profile, but also allows changes to most fields in the base segment of the profile itself, including the default access and the access lists. Failure to control ALTER access authority with IRR.ALTER prefixed profiles in the FACILITY class can mean that users that require ALTER access to a resource are also able to make RACF changes, resulting in separation of duties concerns.

Unauthorized access could result in the compromise of the operating system environment, RACF, and customer data, and the potential of a hacker adding a routine to a library and possibly creating an exposure.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.6 Ensure that access to libraries containing EXIT modules is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering EXIT library data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That EXIT library data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE or READ Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(UPDATE) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access greater than READ UPDATE and higher permits are restricted to: o Systems Programmers

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('EXIT LIBRARY') PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(READ) ID(*) PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS ... (see CIS section 2.4.6)

title: Ensure that access to LINKLIST libraries is controlled
description: The primary function of the LINKLIST is to serve as a single repository for commonly used system modules. Failure to ensure that the proper set of libraries are designated for LINKLIST can impact system integrity, performance, and functionality. For this reason, controls must be employed to ensure that the correct set of LINKLIST libraries are used.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.7 Ensure that access to LINKLIST libraries is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering LINKLIST library data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That LINKLIST library data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE or READ Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(UPDATE) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access greater than READ UPDATE and higher permits are restricted to: o Systems Programmers

To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> ... (see CIS section 2.4.7)

title: Ensure that access to the SYS1.UADS data set is controlled
description: SYS1.UADS is the data set in which emergency user IDs are maintained. This ensures that logon processing can occur even if RACF is not functional. Unauthorized access could result in the compromise of the operating system environment, RACF, and customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.8 Ensure that access to the SYS1.UADS data set is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering SYS1.UADS Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That SYS1.UADS is secured by a profile in the DATASET class that: Has UACC of NONE Is not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(READ) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access greater than READ READ permits are restricted to: o Auditors o Systems Operators o Systems Programmers UPDATE and ... (full steps: CIS section 2.4.8)

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD 'SYS1.UADS' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('SYSTEM USER ATTRIBUTE DATA SET (UADS)') PERMIT 'SYS1.UADS' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD 'SYS1.UADS' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT 'SYS1.UADS' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure that access to system page data sets is controlled
description: System page data sets hold individual pages of virtual storage when they are paged out of real storage. Unauthorized access could result in the compromise of the operating system environment, RACF, and customer data. Page datasets access should be limited to system programmers.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.9 Ensure that access to system page data sets is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering system page data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That system page data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Has UACC of NONE Is not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access READ and higher permits are restricted to: o Systems Programmers

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('SYSTEM PAGE DATA SET') PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure that MCS console access is controlled through profiles in the CONSOLE resource class
description: MCS consoles can be used to issue operator commands. When MCS consoles are configured to force a logon in order to be used, the CONSOLE class protects the logon access. Failure to control access to MCS consoles could result in unauthorized personnel issuing sensitive operator commands.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.10 Ensure that MCS console access is controlled through profiles in the CONSOLE resource class

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that CONSOLE appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that CONSOLE appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that CONSOLE appears. Review the current PARMLIB CONSOLxx members to obtain the list of MCS <console-name>. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the CONSOLE entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no ... (full steps: CIS section 2.4.10)

remediation.command: To activate RACF classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(CONSOLE) To enable generic profile checking for a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(CONSOLE) To RACLIST a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(CONSOLE) To create a CONSOLE profile use the RACF RDEFINE, PERMIT, and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE CONSOLE <console-name> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('MCS CONSOLE ACCESS') PERMIT CONSOLE <console-name> + ACCESS(READ) ID(OPERATOR SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(CONSOLE) Note: You cannot specify the WHEN operand on the RDEFINE and RALTER commands for profiles in the CONSOLE class. To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a general resource profile use the RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER CONSOLE <console-name> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(CONSOLE) Note: You cannot specify the WHEN operand on the RDEFINE and RALTER commands for profiles in the CONSOLE class. To remove a non-compliant access list entry use the RACF PERMIT and SETROPTS commands: PERMIT CONSOLE <console-name> + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH ... (see CIS section 2.4.10)

title: Ensure that access to system USER catalogs is controlled
description: System catalogs are the basis for locating all files on the system. A USER catalog stores the name and location of a data set. The MASTER catalog usually stores only a data set high-level qualifier (HLQ) with the name of the user catalog, which contains the location of all data sets prefixed by this HLQ. The HLQ is called an alias.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.11 Ensure that access to system USER catalogs is controlled

audit.command: Request a list of system USER catalogs from the site. Note: General guidance is that any USER catalog that general users should not be able to modify is in scope of this control. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering system USER catalogs Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That system USER catalog data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE Are not in ... (full steps: CIS section 2.4.11)

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('SYSTEM USER CATALOG') PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(READ) ID(*) PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure that access to Libraries containing EXIT modules is controlled
description: System exits have a wide range of uses and capabilities within any system. Exits may introduce security exposures within the system, modify audit trails, and alter individual user capabilities. Unauthorized access could result in the compromise of the operating system environment, RACF, and customer data, and the potential of a hacker adding a routine to a library and possibly creating an exposure.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4.12 Ensure that access to Libraries containing EXIT modules is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering EXIT library data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That EXIT library data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(UPDATE) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access UPDATE and higher permits are restricted to: o Systems Programmers

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD '<exit-library>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('EXIT LIBRARY') PERMIT '<exit-library>' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD '<exit-library>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT '<exit-library>' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure that SETROPTS CMDVIOL is in effect
description: The SETROPTS CMDVIOL parameter specifies whether RACF is to log violations detected by RACF commands. The improper setting of this field can compromise the security of the z/OS environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1 Ensure that SETROPTS CMDVIOL is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ATTRIBUTES = section. Verify that CMDVIOL appears. Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_AUDIT_CONTROLS) Verify that SETROPTS CMDVIOL is in effect has a Value of YES.

remediation.command: To modify the CMDVIOL parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CMDVIOL

title: Ensure that SETROPTS SAUDIT is in effect
description: The SETROPTS SAUDIT parameter specifies whether RACF is to log RACF commands issued by users with the SPECIAL or group-SPECIAL attribute. The improper setting of this field can compromise the security of the z/OS environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure that SETROPTS SAUDIT is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ATTRIBUTES = section. Verify that SAUDIT appears. Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_AUDIT_CONTROLS) Verify that SETROPTS SAUDIT is in effect has a Value of YES.

remediation.command: To modify the SAUDIT parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS SAUDIT

title: Ensure that SETROPTS AUDIT is enabled for ACTIVE classes
description: SETROPTS AUDIT specifies the names of the classes for which you want RACF to perform auditing. For the classes you specify, RACF logs all uses of the RACROUTE REQUEST=DEFINE SVC and all changes made to profiles by RACF commands. When the class specified is USER, RACF logs all password and password phrase changes made by RACROUTE REQUEST=VERIFY.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure that SETROPTS AUDIT is enabled for ACTIVE classes

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the AUDIT CLASSES = section. Verify that all ACTIVE classes appear.

remediation.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the AUDIT CLASSES = section. Verify that all ACTIVE classes appear. Remediation Procedure To enable AUDIT for all classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS AUDIT(*) Notes: It is generally recommended to activate auditing for all classes via (*) to ease administrative overhead. INACTIVE classes will not generate audit records so there is no disadvantage to enabling the option. If you activate auditing for a class using SETROPTS AUDIT, RACF activates auditing for all classes in the class descriptor table that have the same POSIT value as the class you specify. For example, the classes TIMS, GIMS, and AIMS all have a POSIT value of 4 in their respective class descriptor table entries. If you activate auditing for any one of these classes, you activate auditing for all of them.

title: Ensure that SETROPTS OPERAUDIT is in effect
description: The SETROPTS OPERAUDIT parameter specifies whether RACF is to log all actions allowed only because a user has the OPERATIONS or group-OPERATIONS attribute. The improper setting of this field can compromise the security of the z/OS environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4 Ensure that SETROPTS OPERAUDIT is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ATTRIBUTES = section. Verify that OPERAUDIT appears. Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_AUDIT_CONTROLS) Verify that SETROPTS OPERAUDIT is in effect has a Value of YES.

remediation.command: To modify the OPERAUDIT parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS OPERAUDIT

title: Ensure that SETROPTS INITSTATS is in effect
description: SETROPTS INITSTATS records statistics on all user profiles in the system. INITSTATS records the following: The date and time RACF processes a RACROUTE REQUEST=VERIFY (for example, logon or batch job initiation) for a particular user. The number of RACROUTE REQUEST=VERIFYs for a user to a particular group.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.5 Ensure that SETROPTS INITSTATS is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ATTRIBUTES = section. Verify that INITSTATS appears. Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_PASSWORD_CONTROLS) Verify that INITSTATS in effect has a Value of YES.

remediation.command: To modify the INITSTATS parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS INITSTATS Note: For applications that specify the APPL operand on the RACROUTE REQUEST=VERIFY macro, you can define a profile in the APPL class to specify that the application needs only daily statistics recorded for its users. To do this, specify the RACF-INITSTATS(DAILY) string in the APPLDATA field.

title: Ensure that the assignment of the RACF AUDITOR or ROAUDIT attribute is justified
description: A user having the AUDITOR attribute has the authority to specify logging options, gives control of logging SMF data and list auditing information.. The group-AUDITOR attribute authority is limited to profiles that are within the scope of that group. With the AUDITOR attribute, a user could alter SMF logging data so no trace of the activity could be found. This could destroy audit trace information for RACF system. This attribute should be limited to a minimum number of people.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.6 Ensure that the assignment of the RACF AUDITOR or ROAUDIT attribute is justified

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACUSR Review the AUDITOR and ROAUDIT columns under the ATTRIBUTE TYPE grouping. Verify when SYSTEM or GROUP appears if the assignment is justified for the user.

remediation.command: To remove the AUDITOR or ROAUDIT attributes use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <user-id> + NOAUDITOR + NOROAUDIT To remove group-AUDITOR authority use the RACF CONNECT command: CONNECT <user-id> + GROUP(<group>) + NOAUDITOR

title: Ensure that effective SMF records collection options are set
description: SMF data collection provides a standardized method for recording all system activity to a recording media (file or logstream). including the audit trails from RACF. Some recording options are mandatory to ensure an effective recording of the activity and therefore complete audit trails. If the control options for the recording is not set correctly, system audit could be compromised.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.7 Ensure that effective SMF records collection options are set

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: D SMF,O Look for the following messages: ACTIVE JWT(<hhmm>) MAXDORM(<mmss>) SYS(<options>) Verify that: ACTIVE is present JWT value is equal to or less than 15 minutes MAXDORM specifies a time value of 5 minutes SYS specifies DETAIL

remediation.command: To make changes persistent update the SMFPRMxx parmlib member to use: ACTIVE JWT(0015) MAXDORM (0500) SYS(DETAIL) Note: The two alphanumeric characters, represented by xx, are appended to SMFPRM to identify your SMFPRMxx member. The site should follow their standard procedures for cycling the SMF started task to apply the changes.

title: Ensure that an automated process is in place to collect and retain SMF data
description: SMF data collection provides a standardized method for recording all system activity to a recording media (DATASET or LOGSTREAM), including the audit trails from RACF. Failure to collect and manage adequate retention of SMF records can result in the loss of critical system data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.8 Ensure that an automated process is in place to collect and retain SMF data

audit.command: Review SMF data collection and retention processes. Ensure that the processes utilized include a process which is automatically started to dump SMF collection files immediately upon their becoming full. To ensure that all SMF data is collected in a timely manner, and to reduce the risk of data loss.

remediation.command: Ensure that automated mechanisms are in place to collect and retain all SMF data produced on the system. Dump the SMF files (MANx) in systems based on the following guidelines: 1. Dump each SMF file as it fills up during the normal course of daily processing. 2. Dump all remaining SMF data at the end of each processing day. The same procedure applies if you use LOGSTREAM.

title: Ensure that required SMF data record types are collected
description: 110 0 ~ CICS journaling 110 1 ~ CICS monitoring 110 2 ~ CICS statistics 110 3 ~ Shared temporary storage queue server statistics 110 4 ~ Coupling facility data table server statistics 110 5 ~ Named counter sequence number server statistics 118 TCP/IP Statistics 119 TCP/IP Statistics 123 IBM z/OS Connect EE
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.9 Ensure that required SMF data record types are collected

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: D SMF,O Look for the following messages: TYPE(<{aa,bb|aa,bb:zz|aa,bb:zz,…}>) Verify that at a minimum these types and subtypes are collected: Type Subtype

remediation.command: To make changes persistent update the SMFPRMxx parmlib member to collect the required types. The specific parameter to use will depend on whether a site uses log streams for SMF recording. Note: The two alphameric characters, represented by xx, are appended to SMFPRM to identify your SMFPRMxx member. The site should follow their standard procedures for cycling the SMF started task to apply the changes.

title: Ensure that RACF audit logs is reviewed on a regular basis
description: Logging, the recording of data about specific events, is the key to auditing the use of RACF at your installation. But you also need to ensure the logs are reviewed at least daily. It is very important for any organization to have security logs and actively using them to monitor security-related activities.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.10 Ensure that RACF audit logs is reviewed on a regular basis

audit.command: Verify that site auditors are reviewing RACF event logs (SMF type 80) at least daily, and analyze any security related events. Including but not limited to: invalid access attempts new accounts creation elevation of privileges change of identity access to sensitive resources

remediation.command: Ensure that site auditors are reviewing RACF event logs (SMF type 80) at least daily, and analyze any security related events. Including but not limited to: invalid access attempts new accounts creation elevation of privileges change of identity access to sensitive resources

title: Ensure that only supported software is installed and active on the system
description: When a vendor drops support of software, they no longer maintain security vulnerability patches to the software. Without vulnerability patches, it is impossible to verify that the system does not contain code which could violate the integrity of the operating system environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.12 Ensure that only supported software is installed and active on the system

audit.command: Verify that software products currently installed are still supported by the vendor.

remediation.command: Upgrade the software found at a version less than the current supported version. Replace or remove any software out of support.

title: Ensure all OS software on your system is supported
description: Vendors' code may contain vulnerabilities that may be exploited to cause denial of service or to violate the integrity of the system or data on the System. Most vendors do not develop patches to correct these vulnerabilities on unsupported releases of their software. With unsupported software on the system, it is impossible to verify that the system does not contain code which could violate the integrity of the operating system environment.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.13 Ensure all OS software on your system is supported

audit.command: Verify that site has a formal migration plan for removing or upgrading OS systems software prior to the date the vendor drops security patch support.

remediation.command: Implement a formal migration plan for removing or upgrading OS systems software prior to the date the vendor drops security patch support.

title: Implement sensitive z/OS data set monitoring
description: It is important to monitor changes, additions or removal from APF and LPA libraries, as well as changes to SYS1.PARMLIB PDS members. A monitoring tool should be implemented to monitor the modification to the sensitive z/OS datasets modification. Failure to monitor and review these reports on a regular basis and validating any changes could threaten the integrity and availability of the operating system environment and compromise the confidentiality of customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.14 Implement sensitive z/OS data set monitoring

audit.command: Verify the site is monitoring z/OS sensitive datasets modifications.

remediation.command: Implement a z/OS sensitive dataset monitoring tool.

title: Ensure that SETROPTS REALDSN is in effect
description: If your installation is using the naming conventions table or installation exits to convert data set names, you can specify that RACF put the actual data set names used by RACROUTE REQUEST=AUTH and REQUEST=DEFINE into any SMF log record and operator messages by enabling the SETROPTS REALDSN option. Enabling the REALDSN option ensures that log printouts and operator messages identify data sets by their real names rather than by the data set names that are created by installation exit routines to conform to RACF naming conventions.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.15 Ensure that SETROPTS REALDSN is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Verify the following message is present: REAL DATA SET NAMES OPTION IS ACTIVE

remediation.command: To enable REALDSN use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS REALDSN

title: Ensure that RACF database is backed up on a scheduled basis
description: If backups of the operating environment are not processed, implementation of a contingency plan would not include the data necessary to fully recover from any outage. RACF database backups reduce system recovery time. If regularly scheduled backups of this database are not processed, system recovery time could be unacceptably long.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1 Ensure that RACF database is backed up on a scheduled basis

audit.command: Verify that site RACF databases are backed up at least daily.

remediation.command: Implement a daily backup.

title: Ensure that the RACF PRIM and BACK databases are isolated
description: RACF backup and recovery data files provide the only means of recovering RACF database in the event of its damage. In the case where this damage is to the physical volume on which it resides, and any of these recovery data files exist on this volume as well, then complete recovery of the RACF database would be extremely difficult, if even possible.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2 Ensure that the RACF PRIM and BACK databases are isolated

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: RVARY LIST Verify that the VOLUME values for the PRIM and BACK are different for RACF databases that have YES in the ACTIVE column.

remediation.command: Issue the following TSO command: RVARY LIST Verify that the VOLUME values for the PRIM and BACK are different for RACF databases that have YES in the ACTIVE column. Remediation Procedure Consult the z/OS Security Server RACF Security System Programmer's Guide for guidance on moving the RACF database data sets. Note: Depending upon your configuration, modify the ICHRDSNT load module table or the IRRPRMxx PARMLIB member and plan an IPL of the system (or the entire sysplex if in DATASHARING mode).

title: Ensure that RACF application identity mapping (AIM) is at stage 3
description: Application identity mapping in its final stage, stage 3, is an alternative to the use of mapping profiles to associate RACF user and group names with z/OS UNIX, Lotus Notes, and Novell Directory Services identifiers. For these associations, IRRIRA00 converts the database mapping profile information into an alias index, which uses less space.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4 Ensure that RACF application identity mapping (AIM) is at stage 3

audit.command: Request the SYSPRINT from IRRIRA00 run without parameters, similar to this example job: //DBSTAGE JOB //STEP EXEC PGM=IRRIRA00 //SYSPRINT DD SYSOUT=A Verify that the message returned is: IRR66017I The system is currently operating in stage 3. Alternatively, if IBM Health Checker for z/OS is installed and active, you can request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_AIM_STAGE) Verify that the message returned is: IRRH500I The RACF database is at the suggested stage of application identity mapping (AIM). The database is at AIM stage 03.

remediation.command: Refer to the Security Server RACF System Programmer's Guide for considerations and instructions on using the IRRIRA00 utility to advances the application identity mapping stage for RACF databases.

title: Ensure that RACF ENQ names are not in the Global Resource Serialization (GRS) Resource Name List
description: During its normal course of processing, RACF performs numerous serialization requests using the Global Resource Serialization (GRS) RESERVE, ENQ, and DEQ services. These serialization requests allow RACF to ensure that changes to the RACF database and RACF control blocks are done in a consistent manner, maintaining the integrity of RACF data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.5 Ensure that RACF ENQ names are not in the Global Resource Serialization (GRS) Resource Name List

audit.command: Request the HZSPRINT output for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_GRS_RNL) Verify that the message returned is: IRRH203I No RACF ENQ names were found in the GRS Resource Name List. OR THE CHECK IS NOT APPLICABLE IN THE CURRENT SYSTEM ENVIRONMENT.

remediation.command: RACF resource names are removed from the specified resource name list (RNL) returned by the RACF_GRS_RNL health check.

title: Ensure that SETROPTS GRPLIST is in effect
description: List-of-groups (GRPLIST) authority checking supplements the normal RACF access authority checking by allowing all groups of which a user ID is a member to enter into the access list checking process. This process replaces the checking that compares the current connect group with the resource's access list, and can expand a user's ability to access resources.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.6 Ensure that SETROPTS GRPLIST is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Verify the following message is present: LIST OF GROUPS ACCESS CHECKING IS ACTIVE.

remediation.command: To activate list-of-groups authority checking use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GRPLIST

title: Ensure that SETROPTS NOSTATISTICS(*) is in effect
description: SETROPTS NOSTATISTICS(*) bypasses the recording of statistical information in profiles. We are recommending to bypass resource statistics collection because: Access counts kept only on DISCRETE profiles Counts are not incremented for GAT permitted access or RACLISTed profiles Counts are not accurate in a shared database environment
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.7 Ensure that SETROPTS NOSTATISTICS(*) is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Verify the STATISTICS = section is empty.

remediation.command: To bypass resource statistics collection use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS NOSTATISTICS(*)

title: Ensure that RACF is enabled for Sysplex communication
description: This recommendation is not applicable for systems that are not part of a Sysplex. When RACF is enabled for sysplex communication, it uses Cross-system Coupling Facility (XCF) to join the RACF data sharing group, IRRXCF00. The data sharing group facilitates communication between systems in the sysplex enabled for sysplex communication.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.8 Ensure that RACF is enabled for Sysplex communication

audit.command: Request the HZSPRINT output from each system in a sysplex for: CHECK(IBMRACF,RACF_SYSPLEX_COMMUNICATION) Verify that the message returned is: IRRH343I Sysplex Communication is enabled.

remediation.command: Refer to the Security Server RACF System Programmer's Guide for considerations and instructions on enabling sysplex communication.

title: Ensure that Validated Boot for z/OS is in effect
description: Validated Boot for z/OS is a solution that uses digital signatures to provide an initial program load (IPL)-time check that validates that IPL data is intact, not tampered with, and originated from a trusted source. It also enables detection of unauthorized changes to software executables. By using Validated Boot for z/OS, you have the ability to meet regulatory compliance standards, including National Information Assurance Partnership (NIAP) certification, that are required for certain secure software deployment scenarios.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.9 Ensure that Validated Boot for z/OS is in effect

audit.command: Issue the following console command on each production z/OS system: D IPLINFO Verify the following message is not present: VALIDATED BOOT: NO

remediation.command: Consult the dedicated Validated Boot for z/OS support page.

title: Ensure that the site is registered to the IBM Z and IBM LinuxONE Security Portal
description: The IBM Z and IBM LinuxONE Security Portal currently has Security/Integrity (Sec/Int) APAR information for the z/OS and z/VM operating systems and associated IBM products that ship fixes via PTF, along with critical Security Notices that address hardware, firmware, and software issues. IBM does not make Sec/Int data publicly available for IBM Z.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.10 Ensure that the site is registered to the IBM Z and IBM LinuxONE Security Portal

audit.command: Verify that if the site is an IBM Z client with a need-to-know, at least one person is registered and subscribed to the Security Portal.

remediation.command: The instructions for requesting access to the Security Portal can be found at: IBM Z and IBM LinuxONE Security Portal Registration

title: Ensure that DFSMS is configured
description: Configuration properties of DFSMS are specified in various members of the system parmlib concatenation (e.g., SYS1.PARMLIB). Statements within these PDS members provide the execution, operational, and configuration characteristics of the system- managed storage environment. In the IGDSMSxx member, SMS parameter settings are specified.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1 Ensure that DFSMS is configured

audit.command: Verify the active IGDSMSxx member(s) specifies a minimum of: SMS ACDS(<dataset-name>) COMMDS(<dataset-name>)

remediation.command: To make changes persistent update the IGDSMSxx member to use: SMS ACDS(<dataset-name>) COMMDS(<dataset-name>) The site should follow their standard procedures for cycling the SMF started task to apply the changes.

title: Ensure that access to the Tape Bypass Label Processing (BLP) resource is controlled
description: Tape Bypass Label Processing (BLP) is extremely sensitive, as it allows the circumvention of security access checking for the data. When BLP is used in z/OS, the only verification that is done is for the data set name in the JCL. Any data set name can be used. If an unauthorized user possesses BLP authority, they could potentially read any restricted tape and modify any information once it has been copied.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2 Ensure that access to the Tape Bypass Label Processing (BLP) resource is controlled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the FACILITY entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering the ICHBLP resource Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output ... (full steps: CIS section 5.2)

remediation.command: To activate RACF classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) To enable generic profile checking for a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(FACILITY) To RACLIST a RACF class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY) To create a FACILITY profile use the RACF RDEFINE, PERMIT, and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE FACILITY ICHBLP + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('TAPE BYPASS LABEL PROCESSING (BLP)') PERMIT ICHBLP CLASS(FACILITY) + ACCESS(UPDATE) ID(STGADMIN OPERATOR SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a profile use the RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER FACILITY ICHBLP + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To remove a non-compliant access list entry use the RACF PERMIT and SETROPTS commands: PERMIT ICHBLP CLASS(FACILITY) + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access ... (see CIS section 5.2)

title: Ensure that SETROPTS ADSP is disabled
description: With the SETROPTS NOADSP operand in effect, RACF does not automatically create DISCRETE DATASET profiles when users who have the ADSP attribute create new data sets. IBM recommends the NOADSP option because it reduces the number of data set profiles in the RACF database. Using GENERIC data set profiles is generally more efficient and auditable.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3 Ensure that SETROPTS ADSP is disabled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Verify the following message appears: AUTOMATIC DATASET PROTECTION IS NOT IN EFFECT

remediation.command: To modify the ADSP parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS NOADSP

title: Ensure that access to DFSMS control data sets is controlled
description: DFSMS control data sets provide the configuration and operational characteristics of the system-managed storage environment. Failure to protect these data sets may result in unauthorized access. This exposure could compromise the availability and integrity of some system services and customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4 Ensure that access to DFSMS control data sets is controlled

audit.command: request the following values from the active IGDSMSxx member(s): Source Control Data Set (SCDS) Active Control Data Set (ACDS) Communications Data Set (COMMDS) Automatic Class Selection Routine Source Data Sets (ACS) Active Data set (ACDS) Backup Communication Data Set (COMMDS) Backup These are the DFSMS control data sets. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering DFSMS control data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output ... (full steps: CIS section 5.4)

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('DFSMS CONTROL LIBRARY') PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(READ) ID(*) PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure CSSMTP started task user ID is PROTECTED
description: Protected user IDs are protected from being used to logon to the system and from being revoked through inactivity or unsuccessful attempts to access the system using incorrect passwords and password phrases. However, they can be revoked using the ALTUSER REVOKE command. We recommend assigning protected user IDs to z/OS UNIX, and to the UNIX daemons, started procedures, applications, servers or subsystems associated with z/OS UNIX, to minimize their exposure to inadvertent or malicious misuse or revocation.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1.1 Ensure CSSMTP started task user ID is PROTECTED

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACSPT Use the ASSOCIATED USER column to determine the user ID associated with CSSMTP. Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that the CSSMTP started task RACF user ID: Has the PROTECTED attribute

remediation.command: To make a user ID PROTECTED use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <user-id> + NOPASSWORD + NOPHRASE + NOOIDCARD

title: Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs to CSSMTP started tasks
description: Started procedures have system generated job statements that do not contain the user, group, or password statements. To enable the started procedure to access the same protected resources that users and groups access, started procedures must have an associated user ID. If a user ID is not associated with the started procedure, the started procedure will not have access to the resources.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1.2 Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs to CSSMTP started tasks

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACSPT Verify that the CSSMTP started task(s) appear in the FROM PROFILES IN THE STARTED CLASS: section and not the FROM THE STARTED PROCEDURES TABLE (ICHRIN03): section.

remediation.command: To activate the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(STARTED) To enable generic profile checking for the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(STARTED) To RACLIST the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(STARTED) To create a STARTED profile use the RACF RDEFINE and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE STARTED CSSMTP.* + UACC(NONE) + DATA('COMM SERVER SIMPLE MAIL TRANSFER PROTOCOL (CSSMTP)') + STDATA( + USER(<cssmtp-user>) + GROUP(<cssmtp-group>) + ) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(STARTED)

title: Ensure that access to CSSMTP started task data sets is controlled
description: The IBM Communications Server Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (CSSMTP) STC uses privileged functions and accesses to sensitive data. The data sets CSSMTP relies upon for its configuration, runtime environment and operation must be properly protected from unauthorized modifications or retrieval to ensure system integrity and privacy of sensitive data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1.4 Ensure that access to CSSMTP started task data sets is controlled

audit.command: The data sets to be protected are identified in the data set referenced in the DD statements of the CSSMTP started task(s) and/or batch job(s). Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering CSSMTP STC data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That CSSMTP STC data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have a UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of ... (full steps: CIS section 6.1.4)

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('CSSMTP') PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD '<profile>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT '<profile>' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure SSH daemon is configured to only use the SSHv2 protocol
description: SSHv1 has many well-known vulnerability exploits, and SSH daemons should only use the SSHv2 protocol. Note: Support for SSHv1 was removed from IBM z/OS OpenSSH in z/OS V2R4. This benchmark only applies to z/OS OpenSSH on releases prior to V2R4, or for installations that use a third party SSH implementation on z/OS.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3.1 Ensure SSH daemon is configured to only use the SSHv2 protocol

audit.command: Review all active sshd_config (OpenSSH daemon configuration files). Verify that the Protocol keyword specifies 2.

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating sshd_config configuration files with compliant values.

title: Ensure SSH daemon is configured to use FIPS 140-2 compliant cryptographic provider
description: Use of weak or untested encryption algorithms undermines the purposes of utilizing encryption to protect data. Cryptographic modules must adhere to the higher standards approved by the United States federal government since this provides assurance they have been tested and validated. The FIPS-140 standard requires strict adherence to the use of strong cryptographic algorithms and keys and built-in integrity checks by compliant cryptographic modules.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3.2 Ensure SSH daemon is configured to use FIPS 140-2 compliant cryptographic provider

audit.command: Review the active sshd_config (OpenSSH daemon configuration files). Verify that: The Ciphers keyword list contains ciphers prefixed with aes and without the @openssh.com suffix. The MACs keyword list contains entries greater than hmac-sha-256 Review the active zos_sshd_config (z/OS-specific OpenSSH daemon configuration files). Verify that: The CiphersSource keyword value is ICSF The FIPSMODE keyword value is yes The HostKeyRingLabel keyword is coded The KexAlgorithmsSource keyword value is ICSF The MacsSource keyword value is ICSF

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating sshd_config configuration files with compliant values.

title: Ensure SSH daemon is configured for SMF logging
description: The z/OS OpenSSH daemon can provide audit data in the form of SMF records. The SMF data produced by the OpenSSH daemon provides transaction information for both successful and unsuccessful SSH commands. Failure to collect and retain audit data may contribute to the loss of accountability and hamper security audit activities and use of the SMF data in the execution of a contingency plan could be compromised.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3.4 Ensure SSH daemon is configured for SMF logging

audit.command: Review the active zos_sshd_config (z/OS-specific OpenSSH daemon configuration files). Verify that the ServerSMF keyword value is TYPE119_U83.

remediation.command: Consult the z/OS OpenSSH User's Guide for guidance on configuring z/OS OpenSSH to collect SMF records.

title: Ensure SSH daemon is configured to use SAF keyrings for key storage
description: The z/OS OpenSSH daemon supports the storage of asymmetric authentication keys in SAF key rings or z/OS UNIX file system files. The SSH keys should be stored in SAF key rings to ensure their protection and to provide for organization access control over the keys. The use of SAF Key Rings for key storage enforces organizational access control policies and assures the protection of cryptographic keys in storage.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3.5 Ensure SSH daemon is configured to use SAF keyrings for key storage

audit.command: Review the active sshd_config (OpenSSH daemon configuration files). Verify that any HostKey keywords have been omitted or commented out. Review the active zos_sshd_config (z/OS-specific OpenSSH daemon configuration files). Verify that the HostKeyRingLabel keyword value is coded.

remediation.command: Consult the z/OS OpenSSH User's Guide for guidance on configuring z/OS OpenSSH to setup up server authentication where keys are stored in RACF key rings.

title: Ensure syslog daemon is started at z/OS initialization
description: The Syslog daemon, known as syslogd, is a z/OS UNIX daemon that provides a central processing point for log messages issued by other z/OS UNIX processes. The messages may be of varying importance levels including general process information, diagnostic information, critical error notification, and audit-class information.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.4.1 Ensure syslog daemon is started at z/OS initialization

audit.command: Verify with the site that the syslog daemon (syslogd) is started automatically during the initialization for every z/OS system. Note: syslogd may be started from the UNIX shell, a cataloged procedure (STC), or the BPXBATCH program. Additionally, other mechanisms (e.g., CONTROL-O) may be used to automatically start syslogd. Verify that the WLM service class under which syslogd is classified, is of a high enough to ensure syslogd will not starve for dispatching priority.

remediation.command: Consult the z/OS Communications Server - IP Configuration Guide for guidance on starting and stopping syslogd.

title: Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs with proper parameters to syslog daemon started tasks
description: Syslog daemon, known as syslogd, is a zOS UNIX daemon that provides a central processing point for log messages issued by other zOS UNIX processes. It is also possible to receive log messages from other network-connected hosts. Failure to properly define and control the Syslog daemon could lead to unauthorized access. This exposure may result in the compromise of the integrity and availability of the operating system environment, ACP, and customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.4.2 Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs with proper parameters to syslog daemon started tasks

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACSPT Verify that the syslogd started task(s) appear in the FROM PROFILES IN THE STARTED CLASS: section and not the FROM THE STARTED PROCEDURES TABLE (ICHRIN03): section. Use the ... (full steps: CIS section 6.4.2)

remediation.command: To activate the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(STARTED) To enable generic profile checking for the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(STARTED) To RACLIST the STARTED class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(STARTED) To create a STARTED profile use the RACF RDEFINE and SETROPTS commands: RDEFINE STARTED SYSLOGD.* + UACC(NONE) + DATA('UNIX SYSLOG DAEMON') + STDATA( + USER(<syslogd-user>) + GROUP(<syslogd-group>) + ) SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(STARTED) To make a user ID PROTECTED use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <syslogd-user> + NOPASSWORD + NOPHRASE + NOOIDCARD To modify the OMVS segment for a user ID use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <syslogd-user> + OMVS( + UID(0) + HOME('/') + PROGRAM('/bin/sh') + ) Notes: 1. If the security administrator has defined the SHARED.IDS profile in the UNIXPRIV class, the UID value must be unique. Use the SHARED keyword in addition to UID to assign a value that is already in use. 2. OMVS DIRECTORY and PROGRAM values are case sensitive, so be sure they are entered as-is and not translated to upper case. To add an access list entries use the RACF ... (see CIS section 6.4.2)

title: Ensure permission and user audit bits for syslog daemon component are configured
description: Directories and files of the syslog daemon provide the configuration and executable properties of this product. These directories and files must be properly protected from unauthorized modifications or retrieval to ensure system integrity and privacy of sensitive data. Failure to properly secure these objects could lead to unauthorized access. This exposure may result in the compromise of the integrity and availability of the operating system environment, ACP, and customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.4.3 Ensure permission and user audit bits for syslog daemon component are configured

audit.command: Verify that the permission bits and user audit bits for syslog daemon UNIX files match or are more restrictive than the specified settings listed in the table: File Permission Bits User Audit Bits /usr/sbin/syslogd 740 fff /etc/syslog.conf 744 faf Notes: The /usr/sbin/syslogd object is a symbolic link to /usr/lpp/tcpip/sbin/syslogd. The permission and user audit bits on the target of the symbolic link must have the required settings. The /etc/syslog.conf file may not be the configuration file the daemon uses. It is necessary to check the script or JCL used ... (full steps: CIS section 6.4.3)

title: Ensure that access to syslog daemon archive data sets is controlled
description: syslogd can be configured to automatically archive log files to sequential or Generation Data Group (GDG) data sets. These archive data sets contain log information from multiple z/OS system components and must be properly protected from unauthorized modifications or retrieval to ensure system integrity and privacy of sensitive data.

(full steps: CIS section 6.4.4)

title: Ensure configuration files for the TCP/IP stack are explicitly specified
description: The TCP/IP stack reads two configuration files to determine values for critical operational parameters. These file names are specified in multiple locations and, depending on the process, are referenced differently. Inappropriate values could result in undesirable operations and degraded security. This exposure may result in unauthorized access impacting data integrity or the availability of some system services.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5.1 Ensure configuration files for the TCP/IP stack are explicitly specified

audit.command: Request a copy of all JESJCL of all active site TCP/IP stack started tasks. Note: If a TCP/IP stack is inactive, review the procedure libraries defined to JES2 and locate the TCP/IP stack JCL member. Verify that: The following DD statements appear: o SYSTCPD o PROFILE If a PARM parameter is specified on the EXEC statement and it includes an ENVAR keyword and it specifies the RESOLVER_CONFIG variable: o The RESOLVER_CONFIG value must be set to the same file name specified on the SYSTCPD DD statement.

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating started task procedures to add DD statements or update non-compliant PARM parameters.

title: Ensure TCP/IP stack configuration defined in TCPIP.DATA meets minimum requirements
description: During the initialization of TCP/IP servers and clients, the TCPIP.DATA configuration file provides information that is essential for proper operations of TCP/IP applications. The TCPIP.DATA file acts as the anchor configuration data set for the TCP/IP stack and all TCP/IP servers and clients running in z/OS.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5.2 Ensure TCP/IP stack configuration defined in TCPIP.DATA meets minimum requirements

audit.command: Request a copy of all JESJCL of all active site TCP/IP stack started tasks. Note: If an TCP/IP stack is inactive, review the procedure libraries defined to JES2 and locate the FTP JCL member. Verify that the following parameters are coded in TCPIP.DATA files specified by SYSTCPD DD statements: DATASETPREFIX DOMAINORIGIN HOSTNAME TCPIPJOBNAME

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating TCPIP.DATA configuration files.

title: Ensure hosts identified by the NSINTERADDR statement are protected
description: If the hosts identified by NSINTERADDR statement are not properly protected they can be stolen, damaged, or disturbed. Without adequate physical security, unauthorized users can access the host and the hosts' components. Therefore, they can interfere with the normal operations of the host. Improper control of hosts and the hosts' components could compromise network operations.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5.3 Ensure hosts identified by the NSINTERADDR statement are protected

audit.command: 1. Refer to the Data configuration file specified on the SYSTCPD DD statement in the TCP/IP started task JCL. 2. Gather the following information for any NSINTERADDR statement coded in the TCP/IP Data configuration file: o Identify the physical location of the host running a DNS server (i.e., on-site or off-site at organization, city, state). o Obtain the description of the physical security controls used to limit access to the area where the host is located.

remediation.command: Verify that if the NSINTERADDR statements are not specified in the TCP/IP Data configuration file, this is not applicable. Verify that the NSITERADDR statements specified in the TCP/IP Data configuration file. The NSINTERADDR statements refer to hosts connected directly to networks within the physical premises of the host site. The NSINTERADDR statements refer to hosts that are located in areas with physical access limited to authorized personnel. Ensure that the hosts and the hosts components identified in the NSINTERADDR statement are protected. Ensure that any NSINTERADDR statements coded in the TCPIP.DATA file refer to hosts connected directly to networks within the physical premises of the host site and located in areas with physical access limited to authorized personnel.

title: Ensure TCP/IP stack configuration defined in PROFILE.TCPIP meets minimum requirements
description: The PROFILE.TCPIP configuration file provides system operation and configuration parameters for the TCP/IP stack. Inappropriate values could result in undesirable operations and degraded security. This exposure may result in unauthorized access impacting data integrity or the availability of some system services.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5.4 Ensure TCP/IP stack configuration defined in PROFILE.TCPIP meets minimum requirements

audit.command: This exposure may result in unauthorized access impacting data integrity or the availability of some system services. Note: If an TCP/IP stack is inactive, review the procedure libraries defined to JES2 and locate the FTP JCL member. Verify that the following parameters in PROFILE.TCPIP files specified by PROFILE DD statements: The SMFPARMS statement is omitted or commented out. The DELETE statement is omitted or commented out. The SMFCONFIG statement is coded with ... (full steps: CIS section 6.5.4)

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating PROFILE.TCPIP configuration files.

title: Ensure permission and user audit bits for z/OS UNIX file system objects that are part of the base TCP/IP component are configured
description: z/OS UNIX directories and files of the Base TCP/IP component provide the configuration, operational, and executable properties of IBM's TCP/IP system product. Failure to properly secure these objects may lead to unauthorized access resulting in the compromise of the integrity and availability of the operating system environment, ACP, and customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5.5 Ensure permission and user audit bits for z/OS UNIX file system objects that are part of the base TCP/IP component are configured

description: The Communication Server access authorization is used to protect TCP/IP resources such as stack, network, port, and other SERVAUTH resources. title: Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs with proper parameters to base TCP/IP component started tasks
description: The TCP/IP started tasks require special privileges and access to sensitive resources to provide its system services. Failure to properly define and control these TCP/IP started tasks could lead to unauthorized access. This exposure may result in the compromise of the integrity and availability of the operating system environment, ACP, and customer data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5.8 Ensure that the STARTED resource class is used to assign user IDs with proper parameters to base TCP/IP component started tasks

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that STARTED appears. (full steps: CIS section 6.5.8)

Use the SHARED keyword in addition to UID to assign a value that is already in use. 2. OMVS DIRECTORY and ... (see CIS section 6.5.8)

title: Ensure access to data sets for the base TCP/IP component is controlled
description: MVS data sets of the Base TCP/IP component provide the configuration, operational, and executable properties of IBM's TCP/IP system product. The data sets TCP/IP relies upon for its configuration, runtime environment and operation must be properly protected from unauthorized modifications or retrieval to ensure system integrity and privacy of sensitive data.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5.9 Ensure access to data sets for the base TCP/IP component is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering base TCP/IP component data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That the base TCP/IP component data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(UPDATE) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access greater than READ UPDATE and higher permits are restricted to: o Systems Programmers

title: Ensure VTAM USSTAB definitions are being used for secured terminals
description: VTAM options and definitions are used to define VTAM operational capabilities. They must be strictly controlled. Unauthorized users could override or change start options or network definitions. Failure to properly control VTAM resources could potentially compromise the network operations.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.7.1 Ensure VTAM USSTAB definitions are being used for secured terminals

audit.command: VTAM Systems Programmer supplies the following information: Documentation regarding terminal naming standards. Documentation of all procedures controlling terminal logons to the system. A complete list of all USS commands used by terminal users to log on to the system. Members and data set names containing USSTAB and LOGAPPL definitions of all terminals that can log on to the system (e.g. SYS1.VTAMLST). Members and data set names containing logon mode parameters. Check that the USSTAB definitions are only used for secure terminals (e.g., terminals that are ... (full steps: CIS section 6.7.1)

remediation.command: The Systems programmer will verify that USSTAB definitions are only used for secure terminals. Only terminals that are locally attached to the host or connected to the host via secure leased lines located in a secured area. Only authorized personnel may enter the area where secure terminals are located. USSTAB or LOGAPPL definitions are used to control logon from secure terminals. These terminals can log on directly to any VTAM application (e.g., TSO, CICS, etc.) of their choice and bypass Session Manager services. Secure terminals are usually locally attached to the host or connected to the host via a private LAN without access to an external network. Only authorized personnel may enter the area where secure terminals are located.

title: Ensure that access to the system data sets used to support the VTAM network is controlled
description: Ensure that RACF data set rules for all VTAM system data sets restrict access to only network systems programming staff. These data sets include libraries containing VTAM load modules and exit routines, and VTAM start options and definition statements. Failure to properly control VTAM datasets could potentially compromise the network operations.

If the security administrator has defined the SHARED.IDS profile in the UNIXPRIV class, the UID value must be unique. Use the SHARED keyword in addition to UID to assign a ... The way to ensure the signature verification occurs is by defining a profile in the PROGRAM class with the SIGVER segment. By verifying the IBM generated signature when a module is loaded into storage, the integrity and authenticity of the module are guaranteed.
