title: Ensure ICSF is configured to start during IPL
description: ICSF can be started in different ways, including manual via a START operator command. To ensure maximum availability of ICSF and crypto services, it is best to configure ICSF to be started during the z/OS IPL procedures. This can be done by configuring ICSF to start early as described in Chapter 4. By configuring ICSF to start during IPL, there is less operator manual intervention required, and more availability of crypto services and resources.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.1.4 Ensure ICSF is configured to start during IPL

audit.command: Ensure the IEASYSxx parmlib member has ICSFPROC and ICSF system parameters, e.g.: ICSFPROC=CSF2 ICSF=00 Ensure the ICSF started procedure has been modified to accept the PRM procedure variable, e.g.: //CSF PROC PRM=00 //CSF EXEC PGM=CSFINIT,REGION=0M,TIME=1440,MEMLIMIT=NOLIMIT //CSFPARM DD DISP=SHR,DSN=USER.PARMLIB(CSFPRM&PRM)

remediation.command: Create the ICSFPROC and ICSF parameters in the IEASYSxx PARMLIB member and modify the ICSF started procedure to accept the PRM procedure variable.

title: Ensure that ICSF Master Keys are managed by a Trusted Key Entry (TKE) workstation
description: The z/OS Trusted Key Entry (TKE) workstation allows secure management of IBM Z host cryptographic modules running in (CCA) or IBM Enterprise PKCS#11 (EP11) mode, using hardware-based key management techniques.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.1.5 Ensure that ICSF Master Keys are managed by a Trusted Key Entry (TKE) workstation

audit.command: Verify that the site has a configured TKE workstation, and that ICSF master keys are loaded exclusively through a TKE workstation.

remediation.command: For an interactive starting point and access to a variety of technical resources about z/OS Trusted Key Entry, see z/OS Trusted Key Entry Workstation content solution.

title: Ensure crypto usage statistics are enabled
description: ICSF can be configured to capture statistics related to the use of cryptographic resources, for example key material, cryptographic hardware engines, or even specific cryptographic algorithms. By employing ICSF Crypto Usage Statistics, it is possible to detect the use of crypto resources that are not recommended, such as weak algorithms.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.1 Ensure crypto usage statistics are enabled

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: DISPLAY ICSF,OPTIONS Look for the following message: STATS: Verify the following statistics are collected: ALG ENG SRV

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating parameters in the ICSF installation options data set to update non-compliant parameters.

title: Ensure crypto key lifecycle auditing is enabled
description: ICSF can be configured to audit the lifecycle of key material, for example, key creation, key activation, key deletion, etc. The lifecycle events are recorded using SMF Type 82 records. By configuring ICSF to audit key lifecycle events, it is possible to preserve a record of all major events in a key's lifecycle.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.2 Ensure crypto key lifecycle auditing is enabled

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: DISPLAY ICSF,OPTIONS Look for the following message: AUDITKEYLIFECKDS: Audit CCA symmetric key lifecycle events SYSNAME LABEL TOKEN Verify that the LABEL and TOKEN column values are Yes. Look for the following message: AUDITKEYLIFEPKDS: Audit CCA asymmetric key lifecycle events SYSNAME LABEL TOKEN Verify that the LABEL and TOKEN column values are Yes. Look for the following message: AUDITKEYLIFETKDS: Audit PKCS #11 key lifecycle events SYSNAME TOKOBJ SESSOBJ Verify that the TOKOBJ and SESSOBJ column values are Yes.

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating parameters in the ICSF installation options data set to update non-compliant parameters.

title: Ensure crypto key usage auditing is enabled
description: ICSF can be configured to audit the use of key material, whether or not the key material is stored in an ICSF key data set. By configuring ICSF to audit key usage events, it is possible to document which users and/or jobs are using key material.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.3 Ensure crypto key usage auditing is enabled

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: DISPLAY ICSF,OPTIONS Look for the following message: AUDITKEYUSGCKDS: Audit CCA symmetric key usage events SYSNAME LABEL TOKEN Interval Days/HH.MM.SS Verify that the LABEL and TOKEN column values are Yes. Look for the following message: AUDITKEYUSGPKDS: Audit CCA asymmetric key usage events SYSNAME LABEL TOKEN Interval Days/HH.MM.SS Verify that the LABEL and TOKEN column values are Yes. Look for the following message: AUDITPKCS11USG: Audit PKCS #11 usage events SYSNAME TOKOBJ SESSOBJ NOKEY Interval Days/HH.MM.SS ... (full steps: CIS section 7.2.3)

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating parameters in the ICSF installation options data set to update non-compliant parameters.

title: Ensure ICSF key data sets have a system backup
description: ICSF stores key material in data sets known as "Key Data Sets" (KDS). Symmetric keys (AES, DES, HMAC) are stored in the CKDS, asymmetric keys (RSA, ECC, QSA) are stored in the PKDS, and PKCS#11 tokens and objects are stored in the TKDS. These datasets need to be included in an installation's backup procedure.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.4 Ensure ICSF key data sets have a system backup

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: DISPLAY ICSF,KDS Verify that any KDS data sets listed are included in the system's backup procedure.

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for making updates to the system's backup procedure.

title: Ensure ICSF master keys have a backup procedure
description: In the context of ICSF, a "master key" is a key that is loaded and stored on a Crypto Express Coprocessor, whether configured in CCA mode or EP11 mode. This master key is used to encipher key material when it exists outside the boundary of the CEX coprocessor, and thus is required to make the key material usable.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.5 Ensure ICSF master keys have a backup procedure

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: DISPLAY ICSF,MKS Verify that for any active master keys found there is a procedure in place to backup the value of that master key.

remediation.command: Create a procedure for backing up and restoring the Crypto Express master keys.

title: Ensure all ICSF key data sets are in common record format
description: The format of ICSF Key Data Sets have evolved over time. The most recent format, referred to as "Common Record Format" or KDSR, is recommended as it enables features such as key reference date tracking. The ICSF Key Data Sets must be in KDSR format in order to enable advanced security features such as key reference date tracking.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.6 Ensure all ICSF key data sets are in common record format

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: DISPLAY ICSF,KDS Verify that for any KDS data sets listed the FORMAT value is KDSRL.

remediation.command: The z/OS Cryptographic Services Integrated Cryptographic Service Facility Administrator's Guide provides guidance on using the xKDS CONVERSION utility to convert the record format of a KDS.

title: Ensure all ICSF key data sets are enabled for sysplex sharing
description: When the ICSF Key Datasets are shared among members of a sysplex, it is critical that updates to the data sets are communicated across all members of the sysplex group. To enable the sysplex communication, the ICSF Installation Options Dataset must contain the appropriate sysplex enablement keywords.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.7 Ensure all ICSF key data sets are enabled for sysplex sharing

audit.command: 1. From the ICSF Primary Menu panel, select option 3 OPSTAT. 2. From the ICSF Installation Options panel, select option 1 OPTIONS. Verify that: The SYSPLEXCKDS value is YES,FAIL(YES) The SYSPLEXPKDS value is YES,FAIL(YES) The SYSPLEXTKDS value is YES,FAIL(YES)

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating parameters in the ICSF installation options data set to update non-compliant parameters.

title: Ensure ICSF is running with FIPSMODE enabled
description: If FIPSMODE(YES) is specified in the ICSF Installation Options Dataset, the PKCS#11 services that ICSF provides will operate in compliance with Federal Information Processing Standard Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules, referred to as FIPS 140-2. By operating in compliance with FIPS 140-2, ICSF's PKCS#11 services will ensure the use of strong keys and FIPS 140-2 approved encryption algorithms.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.8 Ensure ICSF is running with FIPSMODE enabled

audit.command: 1. From the ICSF Primary Menu panel, select option 3 OPSTAT. 2. From the ICSF Installation Options panel, select option 1 OPTIONS. Verify that the FIPSMODE value is YES,FAIL(YES).

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating parameters in the ICSF installation options data set to update non-compliant parameters.

title: Ensure CCA operational keys are created with WRAPENH3 key wrapping
description: When the Crypto Express Coprocessor is configured to run in CCA mode, keys generated by the coprocessor are enciphered using the coprocessor's master key (e.g. DES keys are enciphered by the DES master key). The way the keys are enciphered by the master key is referred to as the wrapping method. Creating DES keys using WRAPENH3 will ensure those key blocks are PCI compliant as noted above.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.9 Ensure CCA operational keys are created with WRAPENH3 key wrapping

audit.command: 1. From the ICSF Primary Menu panel, select option 3 OPSTAT. 2. From the ICSF Installation Options panel, select option 1 OPTIONS. Verify that all DEFAULTWRAP values are WRAPENH3.

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating parameters in the ICSF installation options data set to update non-compliant parameters.

title: Ensure that the CSFSERV class is active
description: The CSFSERV SAF class is used to protect access to ICSF callable services and utilities. Users can be permitted or restricted from using ICSF callable services and utilities by enabling profiles within the CSFSERV class.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.3.1 Ensure that the CSFSERV class is active

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that CSFSERV appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that: The CSFSERV entry has: o -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that all profiles in the CSFSERV class: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of FAILURES(READ)

remediation.command: To activate the CSFSERV class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(CSFSERV) To modify the UACC setting for a profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER CSFSERV <profile> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING

title: Ensure that the CSFKEYS class is active
description: The CSFKEYS SAF class is used to protect access to key material stored in an ICSF Key Data Set. Users can be permitted or restricted from access key material by enabling profiles within the CSFKEYS class.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.3.2 Ensure that the CSFKEYS class is active

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that CSFKEYS appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that: The CSFKEYS entry has: o -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that all profiles in the CSFKEYS class: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of FAILURES(READ)

remediation.command: To activate the CSFKEYS class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(CSFKEYS) To modify the UACC setting for a profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER CSFKEYS <profile> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING

title: Ensure that the CRYPTOZ class is active
description: The CRYPTOZ class is used to protect tokens and objects stored in the ICSF Token Data Set (TKDS). Users can be permitted or restricted from access tokens and objects in the TKDS by using resource profiles the CRYPTOZ class.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.3.3 Ensure that the CRYPTOZ class is active

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that CRYPTOZ appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that: The CRYPTOZ entry has: o -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that all profiles in the CRYPTOZ class: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of FAILURES(READ)

remediation.command: To activate the CRYPTOZ class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(CRYPTOZ) To modify the UACC setting for a profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER CRYPTOZ <profile> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING

title: Ensure that the XCSFKEY class is active
description: While the CSFKEYS class controls who has access to key material, the XCSFKEY class provides additional controls regarding how the keys can be used. For example, it is possible to setup profiles in the XCSFKEY class to restrict a keys ability to be used as an exporter or importer key. The XCSFKEY class provides usage control in addition to access permission provided by the CSFKEYS class.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.3.4 Ensure that the XCSFKEY class is active

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that XCSFKEY appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that: The XCSFKEY entry has: o -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that all profiles in the XCSFKEY class: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of FAILURES(READ)

remediation.command: To activate the XCSFKEY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(XCSFKEY) To modify the UACC setting for a profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER XCSFKEY <profile> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING

title: Ensure ICSF key store policy controls are enabled
description: ICSF Key Store Policy governs the use of key tokens in callable services. A key token is just a control block of key material that can be passed directly as an input parameter to an ICSF callable service - as opposed to specifying the label of a key stored in an ICSF Key Data Set. The Key Store Policy settings control how permission to use a key token is performed.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.3.5 Ensure ICSF key store policy controls are enabled

audit.command: Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify the following fully qualified profiles are defined in the XFACILIT class: CSF.CKDS.TOKEN.CHECK.LABEL.FAIL CSF.PKDS.TOKEN.CHECK.LABEL.FAIL

remediation.command: To create general resource profiles use the RACF RDEFINE command: RDEFINE XFACILIT CSF.CKDS.TOKEN.CHECK.LABEL.FAIL + DATA('ACTIVATES ICSF KEY STORE POLICY FOR CKDS IN FAIL MODE') RDEFINE XFACILIT CSF.PKDS.TOKEN.CHECK.LABEL.FAIL + DATA('ACTIVATES ICSF KEY STORE POLICY FOR PKDS IN FAIL MODE') Note: Depending on the RACF class settings you may be required to issue a RACF SETROPTS REFRESH command for updates to be effective.

title: Ensure access to ICSF key data sets is controlled
description: ICSF has three key data sets (KDS) which are used to store cryptographic keys for application use. The three are the CKDS for CCA symmetric keys (AES, DES, HMAC), the PKDS for CCA asymmetric keys (RSA, ECC, QSA), and the TKDS for PKCS#11 tokens and key objects. These key data sets need to be protected to avoid damage or destruction to critical key material.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.3.6 Ensure access to ICSF key data sets is controlled

audit.command: Issue the following z/OS console command: DISPLAY ICSF,KDS Note the names of active ICSF Key Data Sets. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entry covering ICSF key data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that ICSF key data sets are secured by RACF profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(READ) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to ... (full steps: CIS section 7.3.6)

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD 'CSF.KDS.**' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('ICSF KEY DATA SETS') PERMIT 'CSF.KDS.**' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(<icsf-id>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD 'CSF.KDS.**' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT 'CSF.KDS.**' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure access to ICSF operator commands is controlled
description: ICSF has two commands that can be issued at an operator console to display information about ICSF and ICSF resources or make changes to how ICSF is operating: DISPLAY ICSF SETICSF Use of the ICSF operator commands must be restricted to authorized users.

Failure to properly control access to JES2 system commands could result in unauthorized personnel issuing sensitive JES2 commands. If commands are not protected, this may threaten the integrity and availability of the operating system environment and compromise the confidentiality of customer data.

description: JESSPOOL resources control access to data stored on the JES spool data sets. This includes all SYSOUT and instream data set, JCL, SYSLOG, JESTRACE, and JESNEWS data sets stored on spool and the control blocks that represent those data set. If the JESSPOOL class is not active, the integrity and availability of the operating system environment is compromised, and potentially sensitive customer data is exposed.

Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that JESSPOOL appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that JESSPOOL appears.

title: Ensure that access to JES2 trace resources is controlled
description: The JES2 tracing facility can be used to diagnose various problems that can occur in JES2. Since all trace data is intended to diagnose problems with how the system manages data, there are cases where that data may contain sensitive information.

Request a list of all JES2 subsystem IDs used by the site. title: Ensure that RACF is called for data sets opened by JES2
description: The Program Property Table (PPT) provides an option to bypass password checking for data sets (NOPASS). This causes OPEN processing to bypass the call to RACF data set access authorization for the specified address space. JES2 is defined with the attribute PASS which requires that RACF be called for all data set access.

remediation.command: Update the SHEDxx PARMLIB member to remove the NOPASS specification for HASJES20.

If the owner does not have access to the device (as defined by the WRITER resource class profile) then the output is not processed (and remains on SPOOL).

title: Ensure that bypass label processing is not set on any JOBCLASS
description: BLP=YES on a JOBCLASS statement allows certain security checks to be skipped when accessing certain tape data set. There are other ways to manage this setting than the JOBCLASS statement that allow for more granular authorization such as access via the RACF TAPEVOL resource class. Using BLP=YES on a JOBCLASS statement could inadvertently expose data on tapes to unauthorized personnel.

audit.command: Issue the following JES command for each JES2 subsystem: $D JOBCLASS(*),BLP Verify that every JOBCLASS is defined with BLP=NO.

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process to correct non- compliant JES2 initialization statement JOBCLASS entries.

This exposure may threaten the integrity and availability of the operating system environment and compromise the confidentiality of customer data.

audit.command: This guidance addresses RJE Workstations that are "Dedicated". If an RJE workstation is dedicated, the assumption is that the RJE to host connection is hard-wired between the RJE and host. In this case the RMT definition statement will contain the keyword LINE= which specifies that this RJE is only connected via that one LINE statement. Request a list of RMT<nnnn> entries that are "dedicated". Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that any "dedicated" RMT<nnnn> entry has matching RACF USER ID that: Has the RESTRICTED ... (full steps: CIS section 8.7.2)

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS JES(BATCHALLRACF) is enabled
description: SETROPTS BATCHALLRACF specifies that JES is to test for the presence of a user ID and password on the job statement or for propagated RACF identification information for all batch jobs. The system-wide option controls the default settings for determining how RACF will function when handling requests for access to the operating system environment, RACF, and customer data.

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS JES(XBMALLRACF) is enabled
description: XBM (Execution Batch Monitor) is a function that allows jobs to be submitted that only provide instream data to a pre-defined JCL PROC. The classic use of this is to perform student compiles in an educational environment. Even though the JCL PROC is pre- defined, proper auditing of what the JCL is accessing requires that a RACF identify exists for all jobs.

remediation.command: To modify the JES parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS JES(XBMALLRACF)

Improper protection of BPX.SRV SURROGAT resources can result in unintended privilege escalation and loss of accountability.

(full steps: CIS section 9.1)

remediation.command: To activate the SURROGAT class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(SURROGAT) To enable generic profile checking for the SURROGAT class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(SURROGAT) To RACLIST the SURROGAT class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(SURROGAT) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER SURROGAT BPX.SRV.<qualifier> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure that general users are not allowed to change their file ownership
description: By default, only superusers can change the ownership of any file to any UID or GID on the system, and general users can only change the group ownership of files that they own, and only to one of their own associated GID. Only highly trusted users should be allowed to change UNIX file ownership.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.3 Ensure that general users are not allowed to change their file ownership

audit.command: Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that a fully qualified profile named CHOWN.UNRESTRICTED is absent in the UNIXPRIV class.

remediation.command: To remove a UNIXPRIV profile use the RACF RDELETE command: RDELETE UNIXPRIV CHOWN.UNRESTRICTED

title: Ensure that RESTRICTED users cannot access UNIX files to which they are not explicitly permitted
description: A user with the RESTRICTED attribute cannot access RACF protected resources by default mechanisms: the universal access of a profile (UACC), ID(*) in an access list, or the global access table. However, this restriction does not automatically apply to UNIX files. RESTRICTED users may be able to access information they are not intended to have, by virtue of a file's other permission bits.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.4 Ensure that RESTRICTED users cannot access UNIX files to which they are not explicitly permitted

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that UNIXPRIV appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that UNIXPRIV appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that UNIXPRIV appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the UNIXPRIV entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering the RESTRICTED.FILESYS.ACCESS resource Request reports generated ... (full steps: CIS section 9.4)

remediation.command: To activate the UNIXPRIV class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(UNIXPRIV) To enable generic profile checking for the UNIXPRIV class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(UNIXPRIV) To RACLIST the UNIXPRIV class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(UNIXPRIV) To create a UNIXPRIV profile use the RACF RDEFINE command: RDEFINE UNIXPRIV RESTRICTED.FILESYS.ACCESS + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('PREVENT ACCESS VIA UNIX OTHER FOR RESTRICTED USER IDS') SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(UNIXPRIV) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER UNIXPRIV RESTRICTED.FILESYS.ACCESS + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(UNIXPRIV) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the ... (see CIS section 9.4)

title: Ensure that newly assigned UID and GID are unique values
description: When users and groups share UID and GID respectively, they are essentially the same entity to the UNIX kernel. Sharing IDs can result in unintended file access and a loss of accountability.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.5 Ensure that newly assigned UID and GID are unique values

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that UNIXPRIV appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that UNIXPRIV appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that UNIXPRIV appears. Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that a fully qualified profile named SHARED.IDS is present in the UNIXPRIV class.

remediation.command: To activate the UNIXPRIV class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(UNIXPRIV) To enable generic profile checking for the UNIXPRIV class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(UNIXPRIV) To RACLIST the UNIXPRIV class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(UNIXPRIV) To create a UNIXPRIV profile use the RACF RDEFINE command: RDEFINE UNIXPRIV SHARED.IDS + DATA('CONTROL THE USE OF SHARED UNIX UID OR GID')

title: Ensure that z/OS UNIX user accounts are defined with compliant values
description: User IDs, groups, and started tasks that use z/OS UNIX facilities are defined to RACF with an OMVS segment containing attributes such as UID and GID. If these attributes are not correctly defined, data access or command privilege controls could be compromised.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.6 Ensure that z/OS UNIX user accounts are defined with compliant values

audit.command: Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that a USER profile with an OMVS segment has the following attributes: If specified, the UID value must be unique (excluding user IDs assigned UID(0)) If specified, the HOME value must be unique (excluding user IDs assigned UID(0)) The PROGRAM value must be /bin/sh or /bin/tcsh or /bin/echo or /bin/false or other approved value

remediation.command: To modify a USER profile use the RACF ALTUSER command: ALTUSER <profile> + OMVS( + AUTOUID + HOME('</unique/directory>') + PROGRAM('/bin/sh') + ) Notes: 1. AUTOUID is only available if the site has enabled automatic assignment of unique UNIX identities. 2. The HOME and PROGRAM values are case sensitive.

title: Ensure that RACF Classes required to secure the z/OS UNIX environment are active
description: The FACILITY, SURROGAT, and UNIXPRIV resource classes support profiles used to secure the z/OS UNIX (OMVS) environment. UNIXPRIV class profiles are used to manage certain system privileges that are typically associated with z/OS UNIX superuser authority. Without these classes being in active, system integrity can be compromised.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.7 Ensure that RACF Classes required to secure the z/OS UNIX environment are active

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that: FACILITY appears SURROGAT appears UNIXPRIV appears

remediation.command: To activate the classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY SURROGAT UNIXPRIV)

title: Ensure that RACF Classes required to secure the z/OS UNIX environment are RACLISTed
description: RACF provides the ability to load certain classes of profiles into memory for better performance with the SETROPTS RACLIST command. For some classes RACLIST is required, but it does not happen automatically. UNIXPRIV class profiles are used to manage certain system privileges that are typically associated with z/OS UNIX superuser authority.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.8 Ensure that RACF Classes required to secure the z/OS UNIX environment are RACLISTed

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that: FACILITY appears SURROGAT appears UNIXPRIV appears

remediation.command: To activate the classes use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY SURROGAT UNIXPRIV)

title: Ensure that the user account for the z/OS UNIX kernel is defined with compliant attributes
description: User identifiers (RACF user IDs), groups, and started tasks that use z/OS UNIX facilities are defined to a RACF with attributes including UID and GID. If these attributes are not correctly defined, data access or command privilege controls could be compromised. The z/OS UNIX kernel user ID must be defined with only the required UNIX system services attributes and prevented to access online z/OS facilities (ex. TSO, CICS, etc.).
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.9 Ensure that the user account for the z/OS UNIX kernel is defined with compliant attributes

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACSPT Use the ASSOCIATED USER column to determine the user ID associated with OMVS started task. Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that the RACF user ID associated with the OMVS started task: Has the PROTECTED attribute Does not appear on any RACF data set or general resource access list Does not have any segments beyond BASE and OMVS Does not have any extra system or group privileges (ex. ROAUDIT, CLAUTH, group-JOIN, etc.) Has the following OMVS segment values ... (full steps: CIS section 9.9)

remediation.command: To create a compliant UNIX kernel ID use the RACF ADDGROUP, ADDUSER, and CONNECT commands: ADDGROUP OMVSGRP + OWNER(<group>) + SUPGROUP(<group>) + DATA('OMVS KERNEL') + OMVS(AUTOGID) ADDUSER OMVSKERN + OWNER(OMVSGRP) + DFLTGRP(OMVSGRP) + NOPASSWORD + DATA('OMVS KERNEL') + OMVS( + UID(0) SHARED + HOME('/') + PROGRAM('/bin/sh') + ) CONNECT OMVSKERN + GROUP(OMVSGRP) + OWNER(OMVSGRP) Notes: 1. AUTOGID is only available if the site has enabled automatic assignment of unique UNIX identities. 2. The HOME and PROGRAM values are case sensitive.

title: Ensure that z/OS UNIX automount configuration files are configured with compliant values
description: Parameter settings in PARMLIB and /etc specify values for z/OS UNIX security controls, in particular, the automount facility. The automount facility can automatically mount file systems at the time they are accessed, and also unmount them later. The parameters of the automount facility should be set so they are securely mounted by the automount facility, and the users prevented to execute any file from a file-system using the user of the UNIX user or group owner other that file.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.10 Ensure that z/OS UNIX automount configuration files are configured with compliant values

audit.command: Review the logical PARMLIB data sets (ex. SYS1.PARMLIB(BPXPRMxx)) for the following type of FILESYSTYPE entry: FILESYSTYPE TYPE(AUTOMNT) ENTRYPOINT(BPXTAMD) Verify that for any TYPE(AUTOMNT) entries: Each MapName file specifies setuid NO and security YES

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change process for updating non-compliant entries.

title: Ensure that entries in /etc/inetd.conf are active and secure
description: Parameter settings in PARMLIB and /etc specify values for z/OS UNIX security controls. The UNIX services are controlled in /etc/inetd.conf and non-essential and potentially non-secure services must be disabled. The parameters impact HFS data access and operating system services. The /etc/inetd.conf file determines if every entry in the file represents a service that is actually in use. Services that are not in use must be disabled to reduce potential security exposures.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.11 Ensure that entries in /etc/inetd.conf are active and secure

audit.command: Verify that every entry in /etc/inetd.conf represents a service that is actually in use. Verify that the following services have been disabled in /etc/inetd.conf: Service Port chargen 19 daytime 13 discard 9 echo 7 exec 512 finger 79 login 513 nameserver 42 netstat 15 qotd 17 shell 514 smtp 25 systat 11 talk 517 tftp 69 time 37 timed 525 uucp 540

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change process for updating non-compliant entries.

title: Ensure that z/OS UNIX OMVS parameters in IEASYSxx are configured
description: This is a setting in IEASYSxx PARMLIB member to state which BPXPRMxx to use to configure UNIX system services. Parameter settings in PARMLIB and /etc specify values for z/OS UNIX security controls. The parameters impact ZFS data access and operating system services. Undesirable values can allow users to gain inappropriate privileges that could impact data integrity or the availability of some system services.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.12 Ensure that z/OS UNIX OMVS parameters in IEASYSxx are configured

audit.command: The parameter is specified as OMVS=xx or OMVS=(xx,xx,…) in the IEASYSxx member. Note: If the OMVS statement is not specified, OMVS=DEFAULT is used. In minimum mode there is no access to permanent file systems or to the shell, and IBM's Communication Server TCP/IP will not run. Verify that OMVS settings are not defaulting with the OMVS=(xx,xx) parameter set.

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change process for updating non-compliant entries.

title: Ensure that z/OS UNIX BPXPRMxx parameters in PARMLIB are configured for security
description: Parameter settings in PARMLIB member BPXPRMxx and /etc specify values for z/OS UNIX security controls. The parameters in BPXRPMxx and /etc impact data access and operating system services.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.13 Ensure that z/OS UNIX BPXPRMxx parameters in PARMLIB are configured for security

audit.command: Review the logical PARMLIB data sets (ex. SYS1.PARMLIB(BPXPRMxx)). Verify the UNIX parameters are set according to the following table: Keyword Value MOUNT NOSETUID ROOT SETUID SETUID (for Vendor-provided files) SECURITY STARTUP_PROC OMVS STEPLIBLIST /etc/steplib SUPERUSER BPXROOT TTYGROUP TTY UMASK specify that other write bits are not ON USERIDALIASTABLE omitted or commented out

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change process for updating non-compliant entries.

title: Ensure that z/OS UNIX permission bits and audit bits are configured to audit sensitive file access
description: With z/OS UNIX a file owner or a security auditor can specify if auditing is turned on or off, and when audit records should be written for a directory or a file: for successful accesses, failed accesses, or for all accesses. Sensitive files or directories access should be audited. The permissions bits also set access permissions for three classes: owner, group, and other.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.14 Ensure that z/OS UNIX permission bits and audit bits are configured to audit sensitive file access

audit.command: Verify that the permission bits and user audit bits for sensitive files or directories match or are more restrictive than the specified settings listed in the table: File Permission Bits User Audit Bits /usr/lpp/tcpip/sbin/syslogd 740 rwx=f /etc/syslog.conf 744 w=sf,rx+f /etc/hosts 744 w=sf,rx+f /etc/protocol 744 w=sf,rx+f /etc/resolv.conf 744 w=sf,rx+f /etc/services 740 w=sf,rx+f /usr/lpp/tcpip/bin 755 w=sf,rx+f /usr/lpp/tcpip/sbin 755 w=sf,rx+f

remediation.command: To modify the audit flags for a UNIX file use the chaudit command: chaudit rwx=f /usr/lpp/tcpip/sbin/syslogd chaudit w=sf,rx+f /etc/syslog.conf chaudit w=sf,rx+f /etc/hosts chaudit w=sf,rx+f /etc/protocol chaudit w=sf,rx+f /etc/resolv.conf chaudit w=sf,rx+f /etc/services chaudit w=sf,rx+f /usr/lpp/tcpip/bin chaudit w=sf,rx+f /usr/lpp/tcpip/sbin To modify the access permissions for a UNIX file use the chmod command: chmod 740 /usr/lpp/tcpip/sbin/syslogd chmod 744 /etc/syslog.conf chmod 744 /etc/hosts chmod 744 /etc/protocol chmod 744 /etc/resolv.conf chmod 740 /etc/services chmod 755 /usr/lpp/tcpip/bin chmod 755 /usr/lpp/tcpip/sbin

title: Ensure that access to BPX resources in the FACILITY class is controlled
description: The RACF FACILITY class profiles prefixed with BPX are protecting sensitive UNIX System Services capabilities and must be protected. z/OS UNIX RACF-defined resources, prefixed with BPX in the FACILITY class consist of sensitive capabilities including SUPERUSER, daemon, and numerous file manipulation privileges.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.15 Ensure that access to BPX resources in the FACILITY class is controlled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the FACILITY entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering BPX prefixed resources Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 ... (full steps: CIS section 9.15)

remediation.command: To activate the FACILITY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FACILITY) To enable generic profile checking for the FACILITY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS GENERIC(FACILITY) To RACLIST the FACILITY class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(FACILITY) To remove a BPX.SAFFASTPATH profile use the RACF RDELETE command: RDELETE FACILITY BPX.SAFFASTPATH To create catch-all profiles use the RACF RDEFINE command: RDEFINE FACILITY BPX.** + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(ALL(READ)) + DATA('UNIX SYSTEM SERVICES CATCH-ALL PROFILE') SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER FACILITY BPX.<qualifiers> + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FACILITY) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated ... (see CIS section 9.15)

title: Ensure that security parameters in /etc/profile are configured
description: The /etc/profile file is the system-wide profile for the z/OS UNIX System Services shell users. It contains environment variables and commands used by most shell users. Some variables and commands in a secure system. When users are using UNIX System Services through a shell, we must ensure that specific variables are set and specific commands are issued.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.16 Ensure that security parameters in /etc/profile are configured

audit.command: Verify that the following entries have been defined in all active zOS UNIX system services /etc/profile files: umask with a value of 077 readonly with a value of LOGNAME

remediation.command: The site will follow their standard change management process for updating /etc/profile to set compliant values.

title: Ensure that security commands in /etc/rc are safe
description: The /etc/rc file contains customization commands for z/OS UNIX System Services Application Services. Part of theses commands are changing files authorization bits and might change auditing options. Sensitive configuration files or logs must be restricted to authorized personnel and audited for system integrity. Text and must not be changed by application services customization commands.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.17 Ensure that security commands in /etc/rc are safe

audit.command: Verify that any any chmod or chaudit commands targeting sensitive files in active /etc/rc are either removed or configured to set the following values: File Permission Bits User Audit Bits / 755 faf /bin 755 fff /bin/sh 755 faf /dev 755 fff /dev/console 740 fff /dev/null 666 fff /etc 755 faf /etc/auto.master 740 faf /etc/inetd.conf 740 faf File Permission Bits User Audit Bits /etc/init.options 740 faf /etc/log 744 fff /etc/profile 755 faf /etc/rc 744 faf /etc/steplib 740 faf /etc/tablename 740 faf /lib 755 fff /samples 755 fff /tmp 777 fff /u 755 fff /usr ... (full steps: CIS section 9.17)

remediation.command: The site will follow their standard change management process for updating /etc/rc to compliant values.

title: Ensure that each RACF group for UNIX is defined with a unique GID
description: When groups share GIDs, they are essentially the same entity to the UNIX kernel. Sharing GIDs can result in unintended file access and a loss of accountability. Reverse mapping to a group name does not yield a consistent or predictable result, which can lead to confusion in displays such as the output of an ls command.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.19 Ensure that each RACF group for UNIX is defined with a unique GID

audit.command: Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that the RACF groups with OMVS segment values have unique GID values.

remediation.command: To modify the GID value of a RACF group use the ALTGROUP command: ALTGROUP <group-id> OMVS(AUTOGID) Note: AUTOGID is only available if the site has enabled automatic assignment of unique UNIX identities.

title: Ensure that access to data sets used as step libraries in /etc/steplib is controlled
description: The STEPLIBLIST parameter specifies the pathname of the HFS file that contains the list of MVS data sets that are used as step libraries for programs that have the set user id or set group id permission bit set. The use of STEPLIBLIST is at the site's discretion, but if used the value of STEPLIBLIST should be /etc/steplib.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.20 Ensure that access to data sets used as step libraries in /etc/steplib is controlled

audit.command: Request a list of data sets defined in active /etc/steplib. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entry covering data sets defined in /etc/steplib Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that data sets defined in /etc/steplib are secured by RACF profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE or READ Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of SUCCESS(UPDATE) and FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant ... (full steps: CIS section 9.20)

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD '<steplib-dataset>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('CAN BE USED AS STEPLIB LIBRARY FOR SETUID PROGRAMS') PERMIT '<steplib-dataset>' GENERIC + ACCESS(READ) ID(*) PERMIT '<steplib-dataset>' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD '<steplib-dataset>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(SUCCESS(UPDATE),FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT '<steplib-dataset>' GENERIC + DELETE ID(<non-compliant>) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF ... (see CIS section 9.20)

title: Ensure acccess to zFS data sets is controlled
description: z/OS zFS datasets contains z/OS UNIX file systems data. If not protected these datasets can be modified, hindering system security. z/OS zFS datasets contains the files from the z/OS UNIX file systems along with the UNIX attributes controlling security.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.22 Ensure acccess to zFS data sets is controlled

audit.command: Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the DATASET entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering zFS data sets Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify That the zFS data sets are secured by profiles in the DATASET class that: Have UACC of NONE Are not in WARNING mode AUDIT a minimum of FAILURES(READ) ID(*) is not used to grant access UPDATE and higher permits are restricted to: o Systems Programmers

remediation.command: To create a DATASET profile use the RACF ADDSD and PERMIT commands: ADDSD '<zfs-dataset>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('UNIX FILE SYSTEM') PERMIT '<zfs-dataset>' GENERIC + ACCESS(ALTER) ID(SYSPROG) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a DATASET profile use the RACF ALTDSD command: ALTDSD '<zfs-dataset>' GENERIC + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant access list entries use the RACF PERMIT command: PERMIT '<zfs-dataset>' GENERIC + DELETE ID(*) SETROPTS REFRESH GENERIC(DATASET) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL profile and RACF SETROPTS to fully disable GAC for the class: RDELETE GLOBAL <class> SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) SETROPTS NOGLOBAL(<class>)

title: Ensure that the FSSEC resource class is enabled
description: By default, UNIX security attribute (e.g. owner, permission bits) changes are not logged in SMF Type 80 records. These changes should be logged, just as changes to RACF profiles should be logged. In the absence of SMF Type 80 records for UNIX file security attribute changes, it is more difficult to debug authorization problems and investigate potential attacks.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.25 Ensure that the FSSEC resource class is enabled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FSSEC appears. Review the command output in the LOGOPTIONS "ALWAYS" CLASSES = section. Verify that FSSEC appears.

remediation.command: To activate the FSSEC class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FSSEC) Note: Activating the FSSEC class enables the use of ACLs in authorization checking. To enforce logging in the FSSEC class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS LOGOPTIONS(ALWAYS(FSSEC))

title: Ensure that programs cannot execute from the /tmp directory
description: By default, programs and scripts can be run from within any file system in the hierarchy. This ability should be restricted from within the /tmp directory. The FSEXEC class can be used to prevent file execution from an individual file system regardless of permission bits, file ownership, or even superuser privilege.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.26 Ensure that programs cannot execute from the /tmp directory

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FSEXEC appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FSEXEC appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the FSEXEC entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering /tmp Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 output that will allow you to: Verify that a fully qualified /tmp profile is defined in the FSEXEC class that: Has a UACC of ... (full steps: CIS section 9.26)

remediation.command: To activate the FSEXEC class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS CLASSACT(FSEXEC) To RACLIST the FSEXEC class use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS RACLIST(FSEXEC) To create catch-all profiles use the RACF RDEFINE command: RDEFINE FSEXEC /tmp + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + DATA('CONTROL EXECUTE FROM UNIX TMP DIRECTORY') SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FSEXEC) Note: Profile names in the FSEXEC class are case sensitive. To modify the UACC, WARN, or AUDIT settings for a profile use the RACF RALTER command: RALTER FSEXEC /tmp + UACC(NONE) + AUDIT(FAILURES(READ)) + NOWARNING SETROPTS REFRESH RACLIST(FSEXEC) To remove a non-compliant GAC entry you need to use both RACF RALTER and SETROPTS commands: RALTER GLOBAL <class> DELMEM(<entry>) SETROPTS REFRESH GLOBAL(<class>) Note: Access gained via global access checking is not logged, so caution must be used when making changes to GAC entries. title: Ensure that data sets containing user file systems do not have the user ID as the high-level qualifier
description: A naming convention is generally established when allocating new zFS user file systems for a UNIX user to have as their home directory. If the high-level qualifier for this data set is the user's RACF user ID, then the user has read and write access to it outside of the UNIX environment where UNIX authorization checks are not made.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.27 Ensure that data sets containing user file systems do not have the user ID as the high-level qualifier

audit.command: Check the names of the zFS aggregates used for user file systems. The shell df command displays all file systems by path name and by zFS data set name. Verify that the data sets in the Filesystem column containing user file systems do not have the user ID as the high-level qualifier.

remediation.command: Establish a plan by which to replace these file systems. Modify your provisioning steps (for example, your automount policy) to discontinue the user ID-based naming convention in the high-level qualifier.

title: Ensure that daemons are running with z/OS UNIX level security
description: Running with z/OS UNIX level security ensures that system programmers with UID(0) cannot switch identity to any other z/OS UNIX user without authentication. This capability should be restricted to daemon user IDs with READ access to BPX.DAEMON in the FACILITY class. In contrast, with UNIX level security, anyone with UID(0) or access to BPX.SUPERUSER in the FACILITY class can switch identity to any other z/OS UNIX user without authentication. This violates separation of duties and least privilege.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.28 Ensure that daemons are running with z/OS UNIX level security

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the FACILITY entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering the BPX.DAEMON resource Request reports generated using IRRDBU00 ... title: Ensure that servers are running with z/OS UNIX level security
description: Running with z/OS UNIX level security ensures that system programmers with UID(0) cannot establish thread-level security under any other z/OS UNIX user without authentication. This capability is restricted to server user IDs with READ or UPDATE access to BPX.SERVER in the FACILITY class. In contrast, with UNIX level security, anyone with UID(0) or access to BPX.SUPERUSER in the FACILITY class can establish thread-level security under any other z/OS UNIX user without authentication. This violates separation of duties and least privilege.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.29 Ensure that servers are running with z/OS UNIX level security

Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FACILITY appears. title: Ensure that access to file systems containing critical data is controlled
description: Critical data can be stored within zFS file systems. Access to files and directories is controlled by z/OS UNIX mechanisms such as UID(0), file ownership, file permission and access control lists. Using profiles in the FSACCESS class, you can restrict the ability to cross a mount point into a zFS file system to only those explicitly permitted in the profile.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.30 Ensure that access to file systems containing critical data is controlled

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ACTIVE CLASSES = section. Verify that FSACCES appears. Review the command output in the GENERIC PROFILE CLASSES = section. Verify that FSACCES appears. Review the command output in the SETR RACLIST CLASSES = section. Verify that FSACCES appears. Request the following DSMON report: FUNCTION SYSTEM RACGAC Verify that the FSACCES entry has: -- GLOBAL INACTIVE -- or -- NO ENTRIES -- or contains no entries covering file systems containing critical data Request reports generated using ... (full steps: CIS section 9.30)

title: Ensure that file systems are mounted Read Only wherever possible
description: Some zFS file systems contain data that is not expected to change. For example, a file system may be dedicated to containing the binary executables of a specific application. You generally do not expect this data to change until the next time you apply service. Mounting a file system in read-only mode protects against accidental or malicious changes to the data within.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.31 Ensure that file systems are mounted Read Only wherever possible

audit.command: Mounting a file system in read-only mode protects against accidental or malicious changes to the data within. Audit Procedure The UNIX shell command named df displays a list of the currently mounted file systems, by mount point (UNIX directory path) and data set name. Using the verbose option, yields additional information, including the mount mode. Issue the following shell command: df -v The mount mode will be displayed as Read Only or Read/Write. Verify that zFS file systems containing data that is not expected to change are mounted as Read Only.

remediation.command: For each Read/Write-mounted file system in which you don't expect data to change, plan to remount it in Read Only mode as application availability allows, and update the BPXPRMxx member of SYS1.PARMLIB to make the change effective at the next IPL.

title: Ensure that file systems are mounted with set-id files disabled wherever possible
description: set-user-ID and set-group-ID files are those containing executables that run under the identity of the file owner rather than the person running the executable. These are often the target of attackers. On the other hand, some applications rely on these types of files to operate as expected. Mounting a file system in NOSETUID mode reduces the attack surface of your zFS file systems.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.32 Ensure that file systems are mounted with set-id files disabled wherever possible

audit.command: The UNIX shell command named df displays a list of the currently mounted file systems, by mount point (UNIX directory path) and data set name. Using the verbose option, yields additional information, including the mount mode. Issue the following shell command: df -v The presence of the string No SUID indicates the file system is mounted with the NOSETUID option. If it is mounted with the default of SETUID, no option is displayed. Verify that zFS file systems mounted with SETUID have a business justification. Note: Examples of SETUID justification includes ... (full steps: CIS section 9.32)

remediation.command: The shell find command can be used to search for occurrences of set-user-ID and set-group-ID files starting at the path name specified. For example, to see if any set- id files exist in the file system mounted on the /usr/lpp/appx directory: find /usr/lpp/appx -type f \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) Note: The spaces within the parentheses are significant. For each file system in which you don't expect set-id files to exist, plan to remount it with the NOSETUID option as application availability allows, and update the BPXPRMxx member of SYS1.PARMLIB to make the change effective at the next IPL.

title: Ensure that no file systems are mounted with security disabled
description: If a file system is mounted with the NOSECURITY option, everyone has all access to every object in the file system. In a production environment, no file system should be mounted with this option. Mounting a file system in NOSECURITY mode completely nullifies any access control established within it, opening the data for reading and writing to everyone.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 9.33 Ensure that no file systems are mounted with security disabled

audit.command: The UNIX shell command named df displays a list of the currently mounted file systems, by mount point (UNIX directory path) and data set name. Using the verbose option, yields additional information, including the mount mode. Issue the following shell command: df -v The presence of the string No Security indicates the file system is mounted with the NOSECURITY option. If it is mounted with the default of SECURITY, no option is displayed. Verify that zFS file systems are mounted with SECURITY.

remediation.command: For each file system mounted with the NOSECURITY option, plan to remount it without the NOSECURITY option as application availability allows and update the BPXPRMxx member of SYS1.PARMLIB to make the change effective at the next IPL.

title: Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(WARNING) value is set to a minimum of 5
description: WARNING specifies the number of days before a password expires when RACF is to issue a warning message to the user. Note: If you specify WARNING, INITSTATS must be in effect. System users should be warned about impending password expiration to allow secure passwords to be chosen and to allow the changing of a password at a convenient time to help minimize password change impact.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.7 Ensure that the SETROPTS PASSWORD(WARNING) value is set to a minimum of 5

audit.command: Issue the following TSO command: SETROPTS LIST Review the command output in the ATTRIBUTES = section. Verify that INITSTATS appears. Review the command output in the PASSWORD PROCESSING OPTIONS: section. Look for the following message: PASSWORD EXPIRATION WARNING LEVEL IS <nnn> DAYS. Verify the value is equal to or greater than 5 days.

remediation.command: To modify the WARNING parameter use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS PASSWORD(WARNING(5)) Note: If you specify a WARNING value that exceeds the INTERVAL value, a warning message is issued at each logon. If you do not want the warning with each logon, specify a value for WARNING that is less than the value you specify for INTERVAL. If you specify WARNING, INITSTATS must be in effect. To enable INITSTATS use the RACF SETROPTS command: SETROPTS INITSTATS

title: Ensure that access to the warning banner for the FTP server is controlled
description: A logon banner can be used to inform users about the environment during the initial logon. Logon banners are used to warn users against unauthorized entry and the possibility of legal action for unauthorized users and advise all users that system use constitutes consent to monitoring. Failure to display a logon warning banner without this type of information could adversely impact the ability to prosecute unauthorized users and users who abuse the system.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2.6 Ensure that access to the warning banner for the FTP server is controlled

To disable GAC for a class you will need to use both RACF RDELETE to remove the associated GLOBAL ... (see CIS section 6.2.6)

title: Ensure SSH daemon is configured with a logon banner
description: A logon banner can be used to inform users about the environment during the initial logon. Logon banners are used to warn users against unauthorized entry and the possibility of legal action for unauthorized users and advise all users that system use constitutes consent to monitoring. Failure to display a logon banner prior to a logon attempt will negate legal proceedings resulting from unauthorized access to system resources.
reference: CIS IBM z/OS with RACF Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3.3 Ensure SSH daemon is configured with a logon banner

audit.command: Review the active sshd_config (OpenSSH daemon configuration files). Verify that the Banner keyword is coded. Verify that the permission bits and user audit bits for OpenSSH Banner UNIX files match or are more restrictive than the specified settings listed in the table. Permission Bits User Audit Bits 744 faf

remediation.command: The site will need to follow their standard change management process for updating sshd_config configuration files with compliant values. To modify the audit flags for a UNIX file use the chaudit command: chaudit w=sf,rx+f /etc/ssh.banner To modify the access permissions for a UNIX file use the chmod command: chmod 744 /etc/ssh.banner
